5. Wrappers are operated only by trained staff. Operators confirm film roll loaded, turntable and mast guards closed, emergency stop serviceable, and pallet within the 1,000 kg limit and stable before starting the cycle. Film cores, loose wrap and empty pallets are removed to their marks after each pallet so lanes stay clear. Printer and wrapper faults stop the lane until resolved.

6. The 1 cardboard baler handles all waste cardboard from receiving, picking, packing and wrapping. Only clean, dry cardboard is fed, with strapping, film, wood and general waste kept out. The baler area is kept clear and guarded, with bales strapped, labelled and moved to their mark without blocking aisles, crossings, sprinklers or evacuation routes. The baler is never left running unattended.

7. The baler is checked each shift for guards, door interlocks, hydraulics, oil level, emergency stop and bale chamber clear. Feeding follows the safe procedure with two hands clear of the press, and blockages are cleared only with power isolated by the trained operator or the maintenance technician. Any guard, interlock or hydraulic fault tags the baler out until repaired and logged.

8. upkeep is owned by the maintenance technician. He carries out planned checks and repairs on all 8 levellers, both stretch wrappers and the baler, performs immediate repair on tag-outs, and logs every repair with date, equipment, fault and action. Unsafe equipment stays tagged out and parked clear of aisles and docks, and the tag is removed only by the technician after repair and test.

9. Safety, order and handover close the controls. Everyone on the floor wears high-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear, forklift operators wear seat belts when moving, and equipment observes 8 km/h inside the hall and 5 km/h at crossings, pedestrian zones and dock ramps. Open doors, parked levellers, wrapper and baler status, tag-outs and outstanding repairs are recorded in the shift file and carried into the PR-15 handover.

title: Forklift operation
text:
### ops.ch09.s1 Forklift operation

1. Only authorised operators drive powered trucks under PR-10. No person drives a counterbalance forklift, reach truck or electric pallet jack independently until the warehouse manager has authorised that person for that equipment type. No licence, no truck. Authorisation is recorded before first use and is checked by the shift supervisor at every shift start.

2. The powered fleet is all electric with fixed types and roles. The 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t handle general work, horizontal transport and loading, the 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t work only in the high-bay racking in Zone B with its 2,400 pallet positions, and the 8 electric pallet jacks handle horizontal moves in lanes and docks. The 12 hand pallet jacks cover small moves at packing and pick faces. No operator uses a type he is not authorised for.

3. Every truck gets a documented check before its first use each day. The assigned operator inspects brakes, steering, lights, horn, seat belt, forks, chains, mast, wheels, battery charge and leaks on forklifts and reach trucks, and controls, tiller, brakes, wheels and battery on electric pallet jacks. Hand pallet jacks are checked for wheels, forks and hydraulics. The result is recorded with date, truck identity, operator name and signature.

4. Status is re-verified at each shift start. The shift supervisor confirms daily check sheets complete, swaps faulty units, and does not release unchecked trucks to Zones A to F or to docks 1-8. The 20 shared WMS scanners are counted and tested separately so driving checks are not delayed by picking start-up.

5. Any fault stops the truck immediately. The operator parks clear of the 4.0 m main aisles, the 3.0 m rack storage aisles, walkways and dock approaches, tags the truck out, and reports at once to the shift supervisor in charge and the maintenance technician. The truck stays out of service until repaired and logged, and the tag is removed only by the maintenance technician after repair and test.

6. Seat belts are worn whenever the truck is moving, without exception. The operator fastens the belt before moving off, keeps it fastened during travel, placement, retrieval and dock work, and refastens after any dismount. A defective belt is a tag-out fault: the truck is not driven until the belt is repaired.

7. Speed limits are fixed and enforced for all powered equipment. The limit is 8 km/h inside the building and 15 km/h in the 3,500 m2 fenced yard. Wherever people and trucks meet — in marked pedestrian zones, at crossings, and on the dock ramps at the 1.2 m dock height — the limit is 5 km/h. Operators slow to 5 km/h on approach to every crossing, walkway opening, Zone A inspection area, Zone C pick-face ends, Zone D staging lanes and Zone F areas.

8. Trucks stay on their marked routes. Powered travel uses only the 4.0 m main transport aisles for travel, with 3.0 m rack aisles entered only for placement and retrieval. Reach trucks do not leave Zone B racking for general travel, and counterbalance trucks enter rack aisles only to the aisle end. Forklifts do not enter the yard road except to cross at marked points, and pallet jacks do not leave the hall.

9. Driving respects load and site limits at all times. A pallet, load included, may weigh at most 800 kg, each rack bay carries at most 2,700 kg, and free block-stacking is limited to 3 pallets high and 4.0 m. Operators verify bay plates, never carry double pallets or overload attachments, keep loads low and tilted back in travel, sound the horn before blind corners, rack-aisle entry and dock entry, and give way to pedestrians on crossings.

10. Breaches, damage and near-misses stop work and are reported the same shift. Speeding, driving without authorisation, driving without belt, driving a tagged-out truck, or striking racking, barriers, levellers or loads is reported to the shift supervisor, entered in the incident report, and reviewed before the next shift under PR-15. Repeated breach removes driving authorisation pending warehouse-manager review, and open checks, tag-outs and speed incidents are carried into the PR-15 handover.

title: Pedestrian safety
text:
### ops.ch09.s2 Pedestrian safety

1. Pedestrian movement uses only the designated system under PR-11. Pedestrian walkways of 1.2 m width run along the main transport aisles, between Zones A to F, to the office annex, to the marked driver waiting area, and to the assembly point by the north fence. Walkways are physically separated from truck traffic by yellow barriers and are never used for staging, storage, charging or parking.

2. Walkways are kept clear and readable at all times. Floor markings, barrier rails, lighting, mirrors at blind corners and signs at every walkway opening are checked each shift by the shift supervisor in charge. Any damaged barrier, faded marking, blocked section or failed light is reported the same shift to the shift supervisor and the maintenance technician, coned off, and carried into the PR-15 handover until repaired.

3. Powered equipment and pedestrians never share the same lane. Forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks travel only on the 4.0 m main transport aisles and enter 3.0 m rack storage aisles in Zone B only for placement and retrieval. Pedestrians do not step into main or rack aisles except on marked crossings, do not walk alongside moving trucks, and do not enter a rack aisle while a reach truck is operating inside.

4. Crossing takes place only on marked crossings. Crossings connect walkways across main aisles and at docks 1-8, at Zone A inspection areas, at Zone C pick-face ends, at Zone D staging lanes for doors 5-8, and at Zone F packing and quarantine areas. Pedestrians stop at the barrier opening, make eye contact with the driver, wait for the truck to stop, and cross directly without delay or diversion into travel lanes.

5. Every place where people and trucks meet is a 5 km/h zone. Marked pedestrian zones, all crossings, and the dock ramps at the 1.2 m dock height are limited to 5 km/h, against 8 km/h inside the building generally and 15 km/h in the 3,500 m2 fenced yard. Drivers slow to 5 km/h on approach to every crossing and walkway opening, sound the horn before blind corners, rack-aisle entry and dock entry, and give way to pedestrians on crossings.

6. The hall is closed to drivers and uncontrolled visitors. Drivers arriving at doors 1-4 inbound and doors 5-8 outbound remain in the cab during docking or, if required to leave the cab, remain in the marked waiting area and the marked dock-side pedestrian bay. Drivers never enter the hall, Zone A, Zone D or any storage aisle. Visitors move only on walkways under escort and remain in their assigned areas.

7. Everyone on the warehouse floor wears high-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear with no exceptions, including supervisors, stock controllers, dispatchers and escorted visitors. Forklift operators additionally wear seat belts whenever the truck is moving. Persons without correct PPE do not enter walkways or crossings and are stopped by the shift supervisor until equipped.

8. Work areas opening onto walkways are guarded in sequence. Zone A unloading lanes and inspection stations, Zone C scanner staging at aisle ends, Zone D final-check positions and wrapper stations, and Zone F packing stations are set back behind barriers so handling, wrap, pallets and waste do not project onto walkways. Spills, debris, film, strapping and snow, ice or water in the yard are cleared before passage resumes.

9. Breaches stop work and are reported at once. Walking outside walkways, shortcutting through transport or rack aisles, crossing away from crossings, removing or climbing through yellow barriers, or failing to give way are reported to the shift supervisor in charge, entered in the incident report, and reviewed before the next shift under PR-15. Open walkway faults, barrier damage and pedestrian incidents are recorded in the shift file and carried into handover, and repeated breach is escalated to the warehouse manager.

title: PPE
text:
1. Personal protective equipment on the warehouse floor is mandatory and non-negotiable under PR-10 and PR-11. Everyone on the warehouse floor wears a high-visibility vest and class S3 safety footwear at all times, with no exceptions for role, duration of visit or location inside the hall. No person enters Zones A to F, the dock approaches or any walkway or crossing without both items correctly worn and fastened.

2. High-visibility vests are worn closed and visible. Vests are fastened at the front, worn as the outer layer over jackets and workwear, and kept clean so reflective strips remain effective under hall lighting and at dock doors 1-8. Damaged, faded or torn vests are exchanged the same shift. Spare vests are held at the hall entrances for escorted visitors, who remain in their assigned areas on the 1.2 m walkways.

3. Class S3 safety footwear is worn by all floor staff, supervisors, stock controllers, dispatchers on the floor, maintenance staff and escorted visitors. Footwear is laced and fully closed, with toe protection, puncture-resistant sole and water resistance intact. Trainers, open shoes and worn-out or split safety shoes are not permitted on the floor. Persons without correct footwear are stopped by the shift supervisor until equipped.

4. Forklift operators wear seat belts whenever the truck is moving, without exception. This applies to the 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t, the 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t and the 8 electric pallet jacks where a belt is fitted, during travel, placement, retrieval and dock work at the 1.2 m levellers. The belt is fastened before moving off, kept fastened throughout, and refastened after every dismount.

5. Seat-belt serviceability is part of the documented check before first use each day. The assigned operator tests belt retraction, buckle and anchorage with brakes, steering, lights, horn, forks, chains and battery, and records the result with date, truck identity, name and signature. A defective belt is a tag-out fault: the truck is parked clear of the 4.0 m main aisles and 3.0 m rack aisles, tagged out, and reported to the shift supervisor and maintenance technician until repaired and logged.

6. Task-specific protective equipment supplements the floor minimum where the procedure requires it. Cold work in Zone E between +2 °C and +8 °C uses warm, close-fitting layers that do not cover the vest. Hazmat handling and spill response in the 60 m2 ventilated cage under PR-13 uses gloves, eye protection and task PPE as instructed. Baler, wrapper and leveller work uses the guards and interlocks provided, with hands clear of the press.

7. Compliance is checked at every shift start and continuously on the floor. The shift supervisor in charge confirms vests and S3 footwear on everyone present across mornings 06:00-14:00 and afternoons 14:00-22:00, plus any approved Saturday morning overtime, verifies belt use on moving trucks, and stops any person or truck in breach. Drivers remain in the cab or in the marked waiting area and dock-side pedestrian bay and do not enter the hall even with PPE.

8. Breaches stop work and are recorded. Missing or misworn vest, incorrect footwear, or driving without a fastened belt is reported to the shift supervisor at once, entered in the incident report, and reviewed before the next shift under PR-15. The person is removed from the floor until corrected, and repeated breach removes driving authorisation pending review by the warehouse manager. Open PPE faults and issues are carried into the PR-15 handover.

title: Cycle counts
text:
### ops.ch10.s1 Cycle counts

1. Cycle counts run every working day, Monday to Friday, on a rotating zone schedule under PR-08. Stock controllers own the schedule so that Zone B bulk storage with its 2,400 pallet positions, Zone C pick faces, Zone E cold zone, Zone F services including quarantine and the 60 m2 hazmat cage, and open pallets in Zone A and Zone D are all counted in rotation. No working day passes without planned counts.

2. Counts are performed by the two stock controllers with support from the shift supervisor. The daily plan states zone, aisle, rack positions or faces, articles and start time, and is sequenced to avoid blocking replenishment before the picking shift, put-away from Zone A, and loading at doors 5-8. Count tasks fall inside the morning shift 06:00-14:00 and the afternoon shift 14:00-22:00, plus Saturday morning overtime when approved and ordered.

3. Counting runs only on WMS task on the 20 shared handheld scanners. The stock controller scans location label then pallet licence plate, confirms article, quantity, batch and expiry, and posts the first-count result in the WMS without adjusting stock. Pallets are not moved, re-labelled or put away while under count, and forklift operators hold placement and retrieval in that aisle until the count is released.

4. System quantity and physical quantity are compared at the location. If first count matches the system, the location is closed as counted in the WMS and the next location on the rotation is started. Damaged pallets, leaking units, mislabelled cartons, occupied locations and system mismatches found during counting are marked, left in place, and reported to the shift supervisor before any correction.

5. No adjustment is ever posted without a second count. Every difference between first count and system triggers a mandatory recount by a stock controller, independently of the first count, before any stock figure is changed. The recount re-scans location and pallet, re-checks batch and expiry, and checks adjacent locations, pick faces and staging lanes for misplacement.

6. If the second count confirms the first count, the stock controller posts the adjustment in the WMS under PR-08 and records reason, locations, quantities, names and time. If the second count differs from the first, a third check with the shift supervisor resolves which physical quantity is correct before posting. Open differences, unrecounted first counts and held adjustments are never handed over as complete.

7. Damaged, suspect and temperature-abused goods found during counts are handled the same day under PR-09. They are labelled with date, location, reference and fault, moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found, and entered in the quarantine record. Cold-chain stock between +2 °C and +8 °C stays in Zone E unless quarantined, and hazmat stays only in the cage within the 4,000 kg limit and is counted in place.

8. Safety and order apply throughout counting. Everyone on the floor wears high-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear, forklift operators wear seat belts when moving, and powered equipment observes 8 km/h inside the hall and 5 km/h at crossings, pedestrian zones and dock ramps. Counters work only from the 1.2 m walkways with yellow barriers and on marked crossings, and never enter a 3.0 m rack aisle while a reach truck is operating inside.

9. Completion is recorded and handed over. Counts completed, second counts outstanding, adjustments posted and held, quarantine moves, blocked locations and rack damage are entered in the cycle-count log and the shift file and carried into the PR-15 handover. The daily rotation, the two-count rule and the annual wall-to-wall stocktake for manager sign-off together keep system stock equal to stock on the rack.

title: Annual stocktake
text:
### ops.ch10.s2 Annual stocktake

1. The wall-to-wall stocktake is held once a year as a full shutdown count of all stock on site under PR-08. All six zones, A to F, including Zone B bulk storage with its 2,400 pallet positions, Zone C pick faces, Zone E cold zone, Zone F services with quarantine and the 60 m2 hazmat cage, and any pallets in Zone A and Zone D, are counted. No location is excluded.

2. The date is set in advance by the warehouse manager. Inbound deliveries at doors 1-4, outbound loads at doors 5-8, put-away, replenishment and picking are stopped for the stocktake period. The dispatcher closes the dock schedule, trailers on site stay on their assigned door without unloading or loading, and the WMS is frozen so no receipts, issues, moves or adjustments are posted during the freeze.

3. Preparation is owned by the stock controllers with the shift supervisors. Aisles, rack positions, pick faces, staging lanes, quarantine and the hazmat cage are tidied and labelled, blocked locations are cleared or marked, open cycle-count differences are closed or carried forward, and quarantine quantities are confirmed as system-blocked. The 20 shared handheld WMS scanners are charged, tested and allocated to count teams.

4. Counting is performed in paired teams across the two shifts, 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00, plus Saturday morning overtime when ordered for the stocktake. Each team counts only on WMS stocktake task, scanning location label then pallet licence plate and confirming article, quantity, batch and expiry. First-count results are posted without adjusting stock, and counted pallets are not moved until the area is released.

5. No adjustment from the stocktake is ever posted without a second count. Every difference between first count and system quantity triggers a mandatory independent recount by a stock controller, with re-scan of location and pallet, check of batch and expiry, and check of adjacent locations, faces and staging lanes. Damaged, leaking or temperature-abused units found during the count go to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09.

6. Cold-chain and hazmat stock are counted in place without breaking control. Zone E remains between +2 °C and +8 °C with monitoring, alarms and manual verification each shift, and Zone E doors stay shut except for the count in progress. Hazmat stays only in the cage within the 4,000 kg limit. Counters observe 8 km/h and 5 km/h rules for powered support, use only the 1.2 m walkways with yellow barriers, and wear high-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear.

7. The stocktake is closed only with the warehouse manager's sign-off. The stock controllers reconcile first and second counts, list all confirmed differences, postings proposed, quarantine moves and unresolved items, and present the result to the manager. Without that signature the stocktake is not closed, system figures are not taken as verified, and normal inbound, put-away, picking and dispatch do not resume.

8. Reopening is recorded and handed over. Signed results, adjustments posted after second count, quarantine bookings, blocked locations and rack damage found are entered in the stocktake file and the shift file and carried into the PR-15 handover. Only the warehouse manager approves overtime for the stocktake, and the next daily rotating cycle-count schedule restarts from the signed position to keep system stock equal to stock on the rack.

title: Adjustments and racking
text:
### ops.ch10.s3 Adjustments and racking

1. No stock figure is changed without a completed two-count control under PR-08. A first count that differs from the WMS quantity triggers a mandatory independent second count by a stock controller, with re-scan of location label and pallet licence plate, re-check of article, quantity, batch and expiry, and check of adjacent locations, pick faces and staging lanes. Adjustments, corrections and write-offs are never posted on first count alone.

2. Adjustments are posted only by the two stock controllers in the WMS. Once the second count confirms the physical quantity, the controller posts the adjustment with date, time, zone and location, article and quantities before and after, first- and second-count names, and reason code for misplacement, damage, expiry or system error. If second count differs from first, a third check with the shift supervisor decides the correct quantity before posting.

3. Every posted adjustment leaves a full audit trail in the stock file. Cycle-count log, stocktake file and shift file hold counts completed, second counts, quantities posted and held, quarantine moves and blocked locations. Open differences, unrecounted first counts and held adjustments are carried into the PR-15 handover as open, and are never handed over as complete.

4. Quantities blocked in quarantine in Zone F are not available to promise and are never adjusted as available stock. Damaged, leaking, suspect and temperature-abused goods found during counts are labelled with date, location, reference and fault, moved to quarantine the same day they are found under PR-09, and entered in the quarantine record. Stock controllers hold the system block until the final disposition is approved.

5. Write-off approval follows the fixed value limit. The shift supervisor in charge approves damaged-goods write-offs up to and including 500 EUR under PR-09. Any case above 500 EUR is secured, documented and passed to the warehouse manager the same day for sign-off, and no goods are scrapped, removed or written off above that threshold without that signature. Splitting one case to stay below the threshold is not permitted.

6. Racking stays in use only with a documented safety inspection every month under PR-08. The maintenance technician inspects all high-bay racking in Zone B with its 2,400 pallet positions, uprights, beams, bracing, base plates, load plates, beam locks and floor fixings, plus block-stack marks, face and flow-rack frames in Zone C and racking in Zone E and Zone F. The result is recorded with date, area, findings and signature.

7. Load limits are verified as part of every racking check. Each rack bay carries at most 2,700 kg in total, with the site-wide limit of 800 kg per pallet including load, so no bay holds more than three full-weight pallets. Free block-stacking outside racking is limited to 3 pallets high and 4.0 m total height in marked positions clear of the 4.0 m main aisles, the 3.0 m rack aisles, walkways, sprinklers and evacuation routes. Overloaded bays and over-height stacks are unloaded at once.

8. Damage found at any time is reported the same shift. Impact to uprights, beams, bracing, end frames, barriers or load plates by the 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t or the 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t, leaning pallets, collapsed loads or leaking units stop work in that aisle, trigger coning off and tag-out by the shift supervisor and maintenance technician, and are entered in the incident report and repair log with date, equipment, fault and action.

9. Adjustments, write-offs and racking status are closed through handover. Counts posted and held, quarantine bookings, write-off decisions pending manager sign-off, rack damage, tag-outs and the monthly inspection due date are recorded in the shift file and carried into the PR-15 handover. Everyone on the floor wears high-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear, powered equipment observes 8 km/h inside and 5 km/h at crossings, zones and ramps, and counters work only from the 1.2 m walkways with yellow barriers.

title: Returns handling
text:
### ops.ch11.s1 Returns handling

1. Returns are handled only in Zone F services and control under PR-07. All customer returns for the twenty regular clients are accepted, unloaded via doors 1-4 inbound and moved directly to the returns-inspection area in Zone F. No return is inspected in Zone A, stored in Zone B, picked in Zone C or staged in Zone D before inspection is complete.

2. Returns are accepted only within 14 days of delivery. The returns and packing staff of four check delivery date against return request, client, order and article at receipt in Zone F. Returns outside 14 days, without authorisation, or outside packed consumer goods are held apart and escalated the same shift to the shift supervisor and dispatcher without inspection for stock.

3. Every returned unit is inspected individually. The inspector opens, counts, checks condition, packaging integrity, labelling, batch and expiry, leakage, contamination and, for cold-chain goods, temperature evidence between +2 °C and +8 °C. No sampling is permitted. Uninspected units are never restocked, reworked, scrapped or released to any zone.

4. Inspection runs only on WMS task on the 20 shared handheld scanners. The inspector scans return reference, article and location, posts received quantity as blocked stock, and records inspected quantity by condition. Returned quantities stay system-blocked and are not available to promise during inspection. Stock controllers hold the block until final disposition is posted.

5. Damaged, leaking, suspect and temperature-abused units go to quarantine the same day they are found under PR-09. They are labelled with date, return reference, location and fault, moved the same day to the quarantine area in Zone F respecting the 1,000 kg pallet limit, and entered in the quarantine record. They are never re-cooled, racked or picked before a decision.

6. After inspection of every unit, returns staff propose one disposition per line: restock to Zone B, C or E, rework at the value-added packing workstations, or scrap via quarantine. The proposal states quantities, batch, expiry, condition and reason, and is recorded in the WMS and the shift file. No unit leaves the inspection area on the proposer's authority alone.

7. No returned unit is restocked, reworked, quarantined for scrap or released until the shift supervisor approves the final disposition. The supervisor in charge reviews inspection result, proposal and system block, approves restock, rework or scrap, and releases only passed, fully labelled stock with WMS licence for put-away. Cases needing write-off above 500 EUR are secured and passed to the warehouse manager the same day.

8. Approved restock moves as booked stock under PR-02. Forklift operators collect only released, labelled pallets from Zone F, scan them out of returns and into Zone B, Zone E by the closed route with doors shut, or Zone C faces, respecting the 2,700 kg rack-bay limit and the 4,000 kg limit of the 60 m2 hazmat cage where applicable. Hazmat returns stay only in the cage and never in general quarantine.

9. Safety, order and handover close every return. Everyone on the floor wears high-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear, powered equipment observes 8 km/h inside the hall and 5 km/h at crossings, pedestrian zones and dock ramps, and pedestrians use only the 1.2 m walkways with yellow barriers. Open returns, inspections in progress, quarantine bookings and pending dispositions are recorded in the shift file and carried into the PR-15 handover.

title: Damaged goods
text:
### ops.ch11.s2 Damaged goods

1. Damaged goods are controlled under PR-09 from the moment they are found. Any pallet, carton or unit that is crushed, collapsed, leaking, contaminated, mislabelled, past expiry, thaw-suspect or temperature-abused in Zone A, B, C, D, E or F is treated as damaged. It is never racked, picked, packed, staged or loaded as available stock.

2. Damaged goods go to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found, without exception. The finder stops work on that unit, secures the immediate area, and reports at once to the shift supervisor in charge. Inbound operators, pickers, forklift operators, stock controllers and returns staff move the goods the same shift to the quarantine area, respecting the 800 kg limit per pallet including load.

3. Every quarantine move is labelled and recorded at the point of finding. The label states date, zone and location found, door and carrier or order reference where applicable, article, quantity, batch and expiry, and fault description. The move is entered the same day in the quarantine record with time, name and supervisor notified, and scanned as blocked stock in the WMS on the shared handheld scanners.

4. Quarantined quantities stay system-blocked under stock-controller control. The two stock controllers hold the block so damaged stock is not available to promise, not offered to replenishment for Zone C, and not released to Zone B, E or D. No adjustment to available stock is posted without a second count under PR-08, and no quarantined unit leaves Zone F before a disposition is approved.

5. Returns and packing staff inspect quarantined units and propose disposition. After inspection of every unit for condition, packaging, labelling, batch and expiry, and for cold-chain goods temperature evidence between +2 °C and +8 °C, they propose one outcome per line: restock as fully compliant stock, rework at the value-added packing workstations, or scrap. The proposal is recorded in the WMS and the shift file.

6. The shift supervisor approves damaged-goods write-offs up to and including 500 EUR. The supervisor in charge reviews inspection result, proposal, quantities and value the same shift, approves restock, rework or scrap within that limit, and releases only passed, fully labelled stock with a WMS licence for put-away under PR-02. Cold-chain goods are never re-cooled and re-racked, and hazmat stays only in the 60 m2 ventilated cage within the 4,000 kg limit.

7. Any case needing write-off above 500 EUR is secured, documented and passed to the warehouse manager the same day. No goods are scrapped, removed from stock or written off above that threshold without the manager's signature. The quarantine pallet stays locked in Zone F with its record complete until sign-off is given. Splitting one case into smaller amounts to stay below the threshold is not permitted.

8. Spills, leaks, odours and broken packaging stop work in the affected area. The shift supervisor takes charge, triggers containment and the PR-13 spill response for hazmat, calls the maintenance technician, and keeps the area coned off until cleared. Everyone on the floor wears high-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear, forklift operators wear seat belts when moving, and powered equipment observes 8 km/h inside and 5 km/h at crossings, pedestrian zones and dock ramps.

9. All quarantine bookings, inspections in progress, dispositions approved and pending, write-offs passed to the manager, and tag-outs and repairs are recorded in the shift file and the quarantine record and carried into the PR-15 handover. Open decisions are never handed over as complete, and the next shift starts from the blocked position until final approval is posted.

title: Value-added packing
text:
### ops.ch11.s3 Value-added packing

1. Value-added packing is performed only at the packing workstations in Zone F services and control under PR-07 and PR-09. The four returns and packing staff carry out rework, repacking, relabelling and kitting of packed consumer goods for the twenty regular clients. No value-added work takes place in Zone A, B, C or D, and no client stock is reworked without an approved disposition.

2. Only released rework enters the workstations. Returns staff inspect every returned or quarantined unit individually, propose restock, rework or scrap in the WMS, and start rework only after the shift supervisor in charge has approved the final disposition. Damaged, leaking, suspect and temperature-abused goods stay system-blocked in quarantine in Zone F until that approval, and cases needing write-off above 500 EUR stay locked until the warehouse manager signs off.

3. Rework runs only on WMS task on the 20 shared handheld scanners. The task states source quarantine or returns reference, article, quantity, batch and expiry, rework instruction and destination. Operators scan source units out of block, scan new packing and labels during rework, and post completed quantity without adjusting stock outside the task. Stock controllers hold the block until compliant output is posted.

4. All reworked units meet the same standard as new picked stock. Packaging integrity, labelling, article, batch and expiry, count and condition are checked piece by piece, with no sampling. Cold-chain goods between +2 C and +8 C are never re-cooled and re-racked after excursion, and hazmat stays only in the 60 m2 ventilated cage within the 4,000 kg limit and is never reworked to general pallets. Failed units go to quarantine the same day they are found and are entered in the quarantine record.

5. Finished rework is labelled and released as booked stock. Each carton and pallet receives a WMS licence with article, quantity, batch, expiry, rework date and reference, fixed squarely and scan-verified before leaving the workstation. Forklift operators collect only released, labelled pallets, respecting the 800 kg limit per pallet including load and the 2,700 kg rack-bay limit, and scan them out of Zone F to Zone B, Zone E by the closed route, or Zone C faces under PR-02.

6. Workstations are kept set back, clear and segregated. Tables stand behind barriers clear of the 4.0 m main transport aisles and the 1.2 m walkways with yellow barriers, with one job at a time per table, compliant materials separated from quarantined input, and waste removed to its marks. Reworked pallets are never staged in Zone D until packed, labelled, wrapped and released for dispatch.

7. Waste from packing, rework, receiving and picking is handled at source. Only clean, dry cardboard is fed to the single cardboard baler, with strapping, film, wood and general waste kept out. Film cores, strapping, empty pallets and rejected packaging are removed to their marks after each job, with bales strapped, labelled and moved without blocking aisles, crossings, sprinklers or evacuation routes. The baler area stays clear and guarded and is never left running unattended.

8. Safety and upkeep apply throughout. Everyone on the floor wears high-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear, forklift operators wear seat belts when moving, and powered equipment observes 8 km/h inside the hall and 5 km/h at crossings, pedestrian zones and dock ramps. Guards, interlocks and emergency stops on the baler are checked each shift, blockages are cleared only with power isolated, and any fault is reported the same shift to the shift supervisor and the maintenance technician, tagged out and logged.

9. Completion is scan-closed and handed over. Rework completed, labels issued, releases to bulk, cold zone or faces, quarantine moves remaining, baler status and faults are recorded in the shift file and the quarantine record and carried into the PR-15 handover. Open rework, pending dispositions and held adjustments are never handed over as complete.

title: Cold-chain handling
text:
### ops.ch12.s1 Cold-chain handling

1. Zone E is the enclosed chilled store of 300 m2 for temperature-sensitive packed goods only under PR-12. It is held continuously between +2 °C and +8 °C with continuous electronic monitoring, audible alarms and refrigeration on independent power. No ambient goods, hazmat, quarantine stock, packing materials or empty pallets are stored in Zone E.

2. Only booked cold-chain goods enter Zone E under PR-02. Forklift operators collect pallets in Zone A only after the inbound operator has posted the system receipt with temperature evidence, batch and expiry, fixed the WMS pallet licence plate and released the pallet for Zone E. Pallets without a scan-verified label or with missing data stay in Zone A and are never moved to the cold zone.

3. The +2 °C to +8 °C chain is maintained without interruption. The store remains in range at all times, including nights, shift changeovers at 06:00, 14:00 and 22:00, approved Saturday morning overtime, and stocktake freeze. Refrigeration, monitoring and alarms stay active when the hall is otherwise closed and locked. Cold stock is never left on dock ramps, in Zone A lanes, in ambient aisles or in Zone D staging.

4. A manual temperature verification is performed each shift. The shift team reads the independent calibrated thermometer, confirms the continuous monitor reading, checks alarms active and tested, checks doors self-closing with seals intact, and records time, both readings, name and any alarm in the cold log. The shift supervisor in charge does not release Zone E moves until the verification is recorded.

5. Doors are kept closed except for the move or check in progress. Entry for put-away from Zone A, replenishment to Zone C faces, cycle counts on the daily rotating schedule, and verification is one pallet or one team at a time, with doors confirmed shut after each pass. Ice build-up, water, odour, failed lights, damaged seals and door faults are reported the same shift to the shift supervisor and maintenance technician.

6. Cold moves go first and by the closed route. Released pallets travel directly from Zone A to Zone E and from Zone E to Zone C faces or Zone D without staging in Zone B or F, clear of the 4.0 m main aisles and the 1.2 m walkways with yellow barriers. Operators respect the 800 kg limit per pallet including load, scan pallet and location on placement, and feed cold pick faces only from released, in-temperature stock on WMS task.

7. Any deviation stops all work in Zone E at once. Excursion outside +2 °C to +8 °C, alarm, power or refrigeration fault, door left open, or suspect packaging stops put-away, replenishment and picking from Zone E. The team secures the doors, retains stock inside, and escalates immediately to the shift supervisor, stock controllers and maintenance technician. No re-cooling and re-racking of affected units is permitted.

8. Temperature-abused, leaking, thaw-suspect or expired units leave the cold chain the same day they are found under PR-09. They are labelled with date, location, reference and fault, moved the same day to quarantine in Zone F, entered in the quarantine record as blocked stock, and never picked for orders. Replenishment resumes only from stock confirmed in-temperature by the stock controllers.

9. Verification, excursions, quarantine moves, blocked locations and sensor or alarm repairs are recorded in the cold log and the shift file and carried into the PR-15 handover. Everyone entering Zone E wears high-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear with warm layers that do not cover the vest, powered trucks observe 8 km/h inside and 5 km/h at crossings, zones and ramps, and stock controllers post no adjustment without a second count.

title: Hazmat handling
text:
### ops.ch12.s2 Hazmat handling

1. The ventilated hazmat cage in Zone F services and control is the only place hazmat may sit under PR-13. The cage is a separate, locked, ventilated enclosure of 60 m2 within the 600 m2 Zone F, marked, signed and recorded on the site plan. Permitted packed hazmat for regular clients is stored only inside the cage, never in Zone A, B, C, D or E, never in general quarantine, and never on aisles, dock ramps, staging lanes or walkways.

2. The cage holds at most 4,000 kg at a time, without exception. With the site-wide limit of 800 kg per pallet including load, this means at most 5 full-weight pallets in the cage. The WMS blocks any receipt, move or booking that would exceed the cage limit, and inbound operators do not book hazmat without confirmed available capacity. Open cage quantity in kg and pallets is verified each shift and carried into the PR-15 handover.

3. Only booked hazmat enters the cage under PR-02 and PR-13. Forklift operators collect pallets in Zone A only after the inbound operator has posted the system receipt with hazard data, fixed the WMS pallet licence plate with hazard labels readable, and released the pallet for the cage. Pallets without a scan-verified label, with missing hazard labels, safety data, batch or expiry, or with unresolved document discrepancies stay in Zone A and are never moved to Zone F.

4. Hazmat moves go direct and segregated. On release pallets travel directly from Zone A to the cage without staging in any other zone, clear of the 4.0 m main transport aisles and the 1.2 m walkways with yellow barriers. Operators respect the 800 kg pallet limit, scan pallet and cage location on placement, place pallets squarely and fully supported with hazard labels facing the aisle, keep incompatible goods separated by the marked bays, and confirm ventilation running and doors self-closing after each pass.

5. Storage conditions in the cage are maintained continuously. Ventilation runs at all times, including nights, shift changeovers at 06:00, 14:00 and 22:00, and any approved Saturday morning overtime when the hall is otherwise closed and locked. Doors are kept closed except for the put-away, issue or check in progress. Lighting, ventilation, door seals, signage, fire separation and spill kits are checked each shift by the shift team and any fault is reported the same shift to the shift supervisor and maintenance technician.

6. Any hazmat pallet found outside the cage, any damaged, leaking or suspect hazmat unit, and any spill, odour or vapour stops work at once. The finder secures the area, keeps people upwind and clear, and reports immediately to the shift supervisor in charge. The supervisor takes charge of the floor, stops adjacent work, cordons the area, triggers the PR-13 spill response, and calls the warehouse manager, maintenance technician and external services as required.

7. Spill response follows containment, protection and quarantine in sequence. Trained staff wear task PPE for spill handling in addition to high-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear, plus gloves and eye protection as instructed, use only the cage spill kit and absorbents, contain liquid to prevent entry to drains and Zone E, ventilate where safe, and move damaged goods to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found under PR-09. Spilt goods are never re-racked, picked or dispatched, and are entered in the quarantine record as system-blocked stock.

8. Powered equipment observes 8 km/h inside the hall and 5 km/h at crossings, marked pedestrian zones and dock ramps during all hazmat and spill work, and forklift operators wear seat belts whenever the truck is moving. Pedestrians use only the 1.2 m walkways with yellow barriers and marked crossings. Used absorbents, contaminated packaging and failed units are bagged, labelled with date, location, reference and fault, and held in quarantine for decision. No unit leaves quarantine until the shift supervisor approves final disposition, and cases needing write-off above 500 EUR are passed to the warehouse manager the same day.

9. Every hazmat receipt, cage quantity, check, spill, quarantine move and repair is recorded and handed over. The shift file, quarantine record and maintenance log hold time, quantities, names, supervisor review and actions taken, with no adjustment posted without a second count under PR-08. Open cage quantity, blocked quarantine, tag-outs and outstanding repairs are carried into the PR-15 handover, and every spill and breach is entered in the incident report and reviewed by the shift supervisor before the next shift starts work.

title: Emergency evacuation
text:
1. Emergency evacuation is controlled under PR-14 by the shift supervisor in charge. On alarm, injury, fire, spill with vapour, structural damage, power failure affecting safety, or on instruction from the supervisor or the warehouse manager, all work in Zones A to F and at doors 1-8 stops at once. The supervisor takes charge of the floor, stops trucks and dock work, and orders evacuation.

2. Evacuation uses only the marked pedestrian routes. Everyone leaves powered trucks keyed off where safe without blocking the 4.0 m main aisles, leaves dock levellers and wrappers as they are, closes Zone E doors and the hazmat cage doors if on the escape path without delaying exit, and moves on the 1.2 m walkways with yellow barriers and marked crossings to the nearest signed emergency exit. Lifts, shortcuts through rack aisles and re-entry for belongings are not permitted.

3. Everyone on site evacuates, without exception. Floor staff, stock controllers, dispatchers, the maintenance technician, supervisors, managers, drivers from the marked waiting area and dock-side bays, and escorted visitors leave the hall and yard work areas immediately. Drivers leave cabs if in the manoeuvring area and follow the yard pedestrian route. No person stays to finish a pick, booking, load or count.

4. The assembly point is by the north fence. All evacuated persons proceed directly there, remain behind the barrier line, and do not leave the point, enter the yard road, or approach the hall until released. The outgoing route keeps pedestrians clear of arriving emergency vehicles and the 3,500 m2 yard manoeuvring area, observing the 5 km/h shared-area rule for any moving vehicle.

5. Roll call is completed before anyone re-enters the building. The shift supervisor in charge, with the second supervisor or dispatcher where present, calls the roster, shift file, visitor log and driver list, accounts for every person by name, and reports missing persons to the emergency services at once. No search is made by floor staff. The result is recorded with time, names and absences.

6. Re-entry is permitted only after roll call is complete and the area is released. The supervisor confirms with the warehouse manager and the emergency services that the hall is safe, that Zone E monitoring between +2 °C and +8 °C, cage ventilation and alarms are checked, and that aisles, racking, levellers and barriers are intact. No lone re-entry takes place, and work resumes only on supervisor instruction.

7. An evacuation drill is run every quarter under PR-14. The drill is scheduled in advance by the warehouse manager, covers morning 06:00-14:00 and afternoon 14:00-22:00 shift patterns in rotation, and includes alarm activation, evacuation by walkways and crossings, shutdown of the 6 counterbalance forklifts, 4 reach trucks and pallet jacks, dock securing, assembly by the north fence, and full roll call before simulated re-entry.

8. Every drill and every real evacuation is recorded and reviewed. Time of alarm, evacuation time, roll-call result, faults in barriers, markings, lighting, alarms and doors, Zone E and hazmat cage status, and actions taken are entered in the incident report and the shift file. The shift supervisor reviews every report before the next shift starts work under PR-15, and open repairs are passed to the maintenance technician and logged.

9. Everyone on the floor wears high-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear during evacuation and drills, and forklift operators secure seat belts before leaving trucks only where safe to stop. Breaches such as delayed exit, leaving the assembly point, or re-entering before roll call is complete stop the drill or restart procedure, are entered in the incident report, and are escalated to the warehouse manager. Open drill actions are carried into the PR-15 handover.

title: Operator Authorisation and Daily Checks
text:
1. No person drives a counterbalance forklift, reach truck or electric pallet jack independently until the warehouse manager has authorised that person for that equipment type under PR-10. No licence, no truck. Authorisation is separate for the 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t, the 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t for the high bays, and the 8 electric pallet jacks for horizontal moves.

2. Authorisation is recorded before first use. The record states name, equipment type authorised, date of authorisation and the warehouse manager's signature. The shift supervisor in charge checks at every shift start that every driver rostered on powered trucks is on that record. Persons not on the record do not drive, including the 2 floaters, pickers and packers, who use only the 12 hand pallet jacks for their assigned moves unless separately authorised.

3. Authorisation covers only the type stated. A driver authorised for counterbalance forklifts is not authorised for reach trucks or electric pallet jacks, and a driver authorised for electric pallet jacks is not authorised for forklifts. Reach trucks work only in the high-bay racking in Zone B with its 2,400 pallet positions. Any change of type, extended absence, incident or repeated breach requires re-assessment and renewed manager authorisation before driving resumes.

4. Every powered truck and every hand pallet jack receives a documented check before its first use each day. The assigned authorised operator carries out the check and does not hand the truck to another driver as checked. On counterbalance forklifts and reach trucks the check covers brakes, steering, lights, horn, seat belt and anchorage, forks, chains, mast, wheels, battery charge and leaks. On electric pallet jacks it covers controls, tiller, brakes, wheels, horn and battery.

5. Hand pallet jacks are checked in the same routine. The user checks wheels, forks, handle, hydraulics and lowering function on each of the 12 units before first use. The 20 shared WMS scanners are counted and tested separately, so driving checks are never skipped to start picking in Zone C.

6. Each check is recorded with date, truck identity, operator name, result and signature on the daily check sheet held in the shift file. A truck without a completed sheet for that day is treated as unchecked and is not released to Zones A to F or to docks 1-8. The shift supervisor confirms sheets complete at the 06:00 and 14:00 starts and at any approved Saturday morning overtime start.

7. Any fault found at check or during the shift stops the truck immediately. The operator parks clear of the 4.0 m main aisles, the 3.0 m rack storage aisles, the 1.2 m walkways with yellow barriers and the dock approaches, keys off, tags the truck out, and reports at once to the shift supervisor in charge and the maintenance technician. A defective seat belt, brake, steering, horn, light or leak is a tag-out fault with no discretion to continue.

8. A tagged-out truck stays out of service until repaired and logged. The maintenance technician repairs the fault, tests the truck, logs date, equipment, fault and action in the maintenance log, and only he removes the tag. Unsafe trucks are never handed over as available, and open checks, swaps and tag-outs are recorded in the shift file and carried into the PR-15 handover to the next shift.

9. Driving without manager authorisation, driving an unchecked truck, driving a tagged-out truck, or removing a tag without the maintenance technician is a safety breach. It is reported to the shift supervisor at once, entered in the incident report, reviewed before the next shift starts work, and repeated breach removes driving authorisation pending warehouse-manager review.

title: Speed Limits and Driving Rules
text:
### hs.ch01.s2 Speed Limits and Driving Rules

1. Speed limits are fixed for all powered equipment and vehicles on site under PR-10 and PR-11 and are enforced. The limit is 8 km/h inside the building, 15 km/h in the fenced yard of 3,500 m2, and 5 km/h wherever people and trucks meet — in marked pedestrian zones, at crossings, and on the dock ramps at the 1.2 m dock height. No other limit applies.

2. The 8 km/h hall limit governs all travel inside the 6,000 m2 hall. It applies to the 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t, the 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t, the 8 electric pallet jacks and loaded hand pallet jacks on the 4.0 m main transport aisles between Zones A to F and docks 1-8. The 3.0 m rack storage aisles in Zone B are working aisles for placement and retrieval only and are entered at walking pace or less.

3. The 15 km/h yard limit governs the one-way circulation, the trailer manoeuvring area in front of doors 1-8 and the access road. Arriving and departing curtain-side trailers and the delivery van follow the marked lanes clear of the waiting area and walkways. Forklifts do not enter the yard road except to cross at marked points, and pallet jacks do not leave the hall.

4. The 5 km/h rule governs every shared area. Marked pedestrian zones with the 1.2 m walkways and yellow barriers, every marked crossing across main aisles and at docks 1-8, the Zone A inspection areas, the Zone C pick-face ends, the Zone D staging lanes for doors 5-8, the Zone F packing and quarantine areas, and the dock levellers and ramps are all 5 km/h zones without exception.

5. Limits are signposted and readable at all times. Signs stand at the controlled gate, at each hall entrance, at every crossing, walkway opening, pedestrian zone entry and dock ramp, stating 8, 15 or 5 km/h for that area. The shift supervisor in charge confirms each shift that signs, floor markings, mirrors, lighting and yellow barriers are intact, and cones off and reports any missing or damaged sign to the maintenance technician the same shift.

6. Drivers slow to 5 km/h on approach to every crossing, walkway opening, blind corner, rack-aisle entry, Zone A and Zone C work ends, and dock entry, whatever the general limit of the aisle they are leaving. They sound the horn before blind corners, rack-aisle entry and dock entry, keep loads low and tilted back in travel, respect the 800 kg pallet limit and the 2,700 kg rack-bay limit, and never carry double pallets or overload attachments to hold speed on a ramp.

7. Pedestrians have priority in every shared area. Drivers give way to pedestrians on crossings and at walkway openings, stop where sight lines are blocked until the way is clear or the shift supervisor clears passage, and do not overtake, pass a stopped truck at a crossing, or enter an occupied 3.0 m rack aisle without eye contact and horn signal. Pedestrians cross only on marked crossings after eye contact and a full stop of the truck.

8. Seat belts are worn whenever the truck is moving, including at 5 km/h. The operator fastens the belt before moving off on counterbalance forklifts, reach trucks and electric pallet jacks where a belt is fitted, keeps it fastened during travel, placement, retrieval and dock work, and refastens after every dismount. A defective belt is a tag-out fault and the truck is not driven at any speed until repaired.

9. Speeding, leaving the marked 4.0 m and 3.0 m routes, driving through or removing yellow barriers, failing to slow at crossings and ramps, or failing to give way is a safety breach. It is reported at once to the shift supervisor in charge, entered in the incident report, reviewed before the next shift starts work under PR-15, and carried into the handover. Repeated breach removes driving authorisation pending review by the warehouse manager.

title: Pedestrian Walkways and Conduct
text:
### hs.ch01.s3 Pedestrian Walkways and Conduct

1. Pedestrians move only on the designated walkway system under PR-11. Walkways of 1.2 m width run along the 4.0 m main transport aisles, between Zones A to F, to the office annex, to the marked driver waiting area, and to the assembly point by the north fence. Walkways are physically separated from truck traffic by yellow barriers and are never used for staging, storage, charging, parking or pallet stacks.

2. Walkways are kept clear, lit and readable at all times. Floor markings, barrier rails, mirrors at blind corners, lighting and signs at every walkway opening are checked each shift by the shift supervisor in charge. Any damaged barrier, faded marking, blocked section or failed light is coned off, reported the same shift to the shift supervisor and the maintenance technician, and carried into the PR-15 handover until repaired.

3. Powered equipment and pedestrians never share the same lane. The 6 counterbalance forklifts, 4 reach trucks and 8 electric pallet jacks travel only on main aisles and enter the 3.0 m rack storage aisles in Zone B only for placement and retrieval. Pedestrians do not step into main or rack aisles except on marked crossings, do not walk alongside moving trucks, and do not enter a rack aisle while a reach truck is operating inside.

4. Crossing takes place only on marked crossings. Crossings connect walkways across main aisles and at docks 1-8, at the Zone A inspection areas, at the Zone C pick-face ends, at the Zone D staging lanes for doors 5-8, and at the Zone F packing and quarantine areas. Pedestrians stop at the barrier opening, make eye contact with the driver, wait for the truck to come to a full stop, and cross directly without delay or diversion into travel lanes.

5. Every place where people and trucks meet is a 5 km/h zone. Marked pedestrian zones, all crossings, and the dock ramps at the 1.2 m dock height are limited to 5 km/h, against 8 km/h inside the building generally and 15 km/h in the fenced yard. Drivers slow to 5 km/h on approach to every crossing and walkway opening, sound the horn before blind corners, rack-aisle entry and dock entry, and give way to pedestrians on crossings.

6. The hall is closed to drivers and uncontrolled visitors. Drivers arriving at doors 1-4 inbound and doors 5-8 outbound remain in the cab during docking or, if required to leave the cab, remain in the marked waiting area and the marked dock-side pedestrian bay. Drivers never enter the hall, Zone A, Zone D or any storage aisle. Visitors move only on the 1.2 m walkways under escort and remain in assigned areas.

7. Everyone on the warehouse floor wears a high-visibility vest and class S3 safety footwear with no exceptions, including supervisors, stock controllers, dispatchers on the floor and escorted visitors. Forklift operators additionally wear seat belts whenever the truck is moving. Persons without correct PPE do not enter walkways or crossings and are stopped by the shift supervisor until equipped.

8. Work areas opening onto walkways are set back behind barriers. Zone A unloading lanes and inspection stations, Zone C scanner staging at aisle ends, Zone D final-check positions and wrapper stations, and Zone F packing stations are arranged so handling, wrap, pallets and waste do not project onto walkways. Spills, debris, film, strapping and snow, ice or water in the yard are cleared before pedestrian passage resumes.

9. Breaches stop work and are reported at once. Walking outside walkways, shortcutting through transport or rack aisles, crossing away from crossings, removing or climbing through yellow barriers, or failing to give way are reported to the shift supervisor in charge, entered in the incident report, and reviewed before the next shift starts work under PR-15. Open walkway faults, barrier damage and pedestrian incidents are recorded in the shift file and carried into handover, and repeated breach is escalated to the warehouse manager.

title: Mandatory PPE
text:
1. Personal protective equipment on the warehouse floor is mandatory and non-negotiable under PR-10 and PR-11. Everyone on the warehouse floor wears a high-visibility vest and class S3 safety footwear at all times, with no exceptions for role, duration of visit or location inside the hall. No person enters Zones A to F, the dock approaches at doors 1-8, or any 1.2 m walkway or marked crossing without both items correctly worn and fastened.

2. High-visibility vests are worn closed and visible as the outer layer. Vests are fastened at the front, worn over jackets, fleece and cold-zone layers without covering the reflective strips, and kept clean so they remain effective under hall lighting and at the docks. Damaged, faded or torn vests are exchanged the same shift. Spare vests are held at the hall entrances for escorted visitors, who remain in their assigned areas on the walkways.

3. Class S3 safety footwear is worn by all floor staff, shift supervisors, stock controllers, dispatchers on the floor, the maintenance technician and escorted visitors. Footwear is laced and fully closed, with toe protection, puncture-resistant sole and water resistance intact. Trainers, open shoes, sandals and worn-out, split or otherwise failed safety shoes are not permitted on the floor. Persons without correct footwear are stopped by the shift supervisor in charge until equipped.

4. Forklift operators wear seat belts whenever the truck is moving, without exception. This applies to the 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t, the 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t in Zone B, and the 8 electric pallet jacks where a belt is fitted, during travel on the 4.0 m main aisles, work in the 3.0 m rack aisles, and dock work at the 1.2 m levellers. The belt is fastened before moving off, kept fastened throughout travel, placement, retrieval and loading, and refastened after every dismount, including at 5 km/h in shared areas.

5. Seat-belt serviceability is part of the documented check before first use each day. The assigned authorised operator tests belt retraction, buckle and anchorage together with brakes, steering, lights, horn, forks, chains, wheels, battery and leaks, and records the result with date, truck identity, name and signature on the daily check sheet. A defective belt is a tag-out fault with no discretion to continue: the truck is parked clear of aisles, walkways and dock approaches, keyed off, tagged out, and reported to the shift supervisor and maintenance technician until repaired and logged.

6. Task-specific equipment supplements the floor minimum and never replaces it. Cold work in Zone E between +2 °C and +8 °C uses warm, close-fitting layers that do not cover the vest. Hazmat handling and spill response in the 60 m2 ventilated cage under PR-13 uses gloves, eye protection and task PPE as instructed. Baler, wrapper and leveller work uses the guards and interlocks provided, with hands clear of moving parts.

7. Compliance is checked at every shift start and continuously on the floor. The shift supervisor in charge confirms vests and S3 footwear on everyone present across mornings 06:00-14:00 and afternoons 14:00-22:00, plus any approved Saturday morning overtime, verifies belt use on moving trucks, and stops any person or truck in breach. Drivers remain in the cab or in the marked waiting area and dock-side pedestrian bay and do not enter the hall even with PPE, and visitors move only on walkways under escort.

8. Breaches stop work and are recorded. Missing or misworn vest, incorrect footwear, or driving without a fastened belt is reported to the shift supervisor at once, entered in the incident report, and reviewed before the next shift starts work under PR-15. The person is removed from the floor until corrected, and the truck is not driven until the belt is repaired. Repeated breach removes driving authorisation pending review by the warehouse manager, and open PPE faults are carried into the PR-15 handover.

title: Cold Zone Rules
text:
### hs.ch02.s2 Cold Zone Rules

1. Zone E is the enclosed chilled store of 300 m2 for temperature-sensitive packed goods only under PR-12. It is held continuously between +2 °C and +8 °C with continuous electronic monitoring, audible alarms and refrigeration that remain active at all times, including nights, shift changeovers at 06:00, 14:00 and 22:00, and any approved Saturday morning overtime when the hall is otherwise closed and locked.

2. No other goods or activities enter Zone E. Ambient goods, hazmat, quarantine stock, packing materials, empty pallets and waste are never stored or staged in the cold zone. Only booked cold-chain pallets with system receipt, temperature evidence, batch and expiry, and a scan-verified WMS pallet licence plate enter Zone E under PR-02, and only released, in-temperature stock is replenished to Zone C pick faces or picked for orders.

3. A manual temperature verification is performed each shift and recorded in the cold log. The shift team reads the independent calibrated thermometer, compares it with the continuous monitor reading, confirms audible alarms active, checks doors self-closing with seals intact, lights working and no ice, water, odour or packaging failure, and records time, both readings, name and any alarm. The shift supervisor in charge does not release Zone E moves until the verification is recorded.

4. Doors are kept closed except for the move or check in progress. Entry for put-away from Zone A, replenishment to Zone C, cycle counts on the daily rotating schedule and verification is one pallet or one team at a time, with doors confirmed shut after each pass. Cold stock is never left on dock ramps, in Zone A lanes, in ambient aisles or in Zone D staging, and cold moves go first and direct by the closed route.

5. Safe work in the cold zone supplements the floor PPE minimum and never replaces it. Everyone entering wears a high-visibility vest and class S3 safety footwear with no exceptions, plus warm, close-fitting layers that do not cover the reflective strips of the vest. Wet floors from condensation or ice, reduced dexterity in the cold, and fogged eyewear are reported at once, and affected areas are cleared and dried before passage or handling resumes.

6. Powered trucks in and around Zone E observe the fixed traffic system. Operators respect the site-wide limit of 800 kg per pallet including load, travel at 8 km/h inside the hall and 5 km/h at crossings, marked pedestrian zones and dock ramps, use only the 4.0 m main aisles and the 1.2 m walkways with yellow barriers, and wear seat belts whenever the truck is moving. Pallets are placed squarely and fully supported with labels facing the aisle, and are scanned at pallet and location on placement.

7. Any deviation stops all work in Zone E at once. Excursion outside +2 °C to +8 °C, alarm, power or refrigeration fault, door left open or not sealing, ice build-up, water ingress or suspect packaging stops put-away, replenishment and picking from Zone E. The team secures the doors, retains stock inside, and escalates immediately to the shift supervisor in charge, the stock controllers and the maintenance technician.

8. Temperature-abused, leaking, thaw-suspect or expired units leave the cold chain the same day they are found under PR-09. They are labelled with date, location, reference and fault, moved the same day to quarantine in Zone F, entered in the quarantine record as system-blocked stock, and never re-cooled, re-racked in Zone E or picked for orders. Replenishment and picking resume only from stock confirmed in-temperature by the stock controllers.

9. Verification results, excursions, quarantine moves, blocked locations and sensor, door or alarm faults are recorded in the cold log and the shift file and carried into the PR-15 handover. Faults are reported the same shift to the shift supervisor and the maintenance technician, logged with date, equipment, fault and action, and the area stays secured until repaired and tested. No adjustment in Zone E is posted without a second count under PR-08.

title: Site Layout and Dock Discipline
text:
### hs.ch02.s3 Site Layout and Dock Discipline

1. The Port Sellow site is one single-storey hall of 6,000 m2 with 10 m clear height, plus a small office annex, inside a fenced yard of about 3,500 m2. All goods handling stays inside the six fixed zones, A to F. No storage, staging or handling takes place outside its assigned zone, and goods move only in sequence from receiving through storage and picking to dispatch.

2. Zone A — receiving, 800 m2, lies along inbound docks 1-4 and holds unloading lanes, inspection tables and booking points. Nothing leaves Zone A until documents are checked, quantities counted, condition inspected and receipt booked. Zone B — bulk storage, 2,200 m2, holds high-bay racking with 2,400 pallet positions and marked block-stack positions. Zone C — picking, 1,200 m2, holds ground-level pick faces and flow racks fed from bulk.

3. Zone D — dispatch, 900 m2, lies in front of outbound docks 5-8 and holds marked staging lanes per door and wrapping stations. Only wrapped, labelled and system-released pallets are staged there. Zone E — cold zone, 300 m2, is the enclosed chilled store held between +2 °C and +8 °C. Zone F — services and control, 600 m2, holds value-added packing, quarantine, returns inspection and the separate ventilated hazmat cage of 60 m2, the only place hazmat may sit.

4. Dock directions are strictly separated. Doors 1-4 are inbound only and open into Zone A. Doors 5-8 are outbound only and open from Zone D. No inbound unloading takes place at doors 5-8 and no outbound loading at doors 1-4. Separation is marked on the floor, on the doors inside and outside, and on the site plan at the gate.

5. Every vehicle movement is assigned in advance by the dispatcher, who books transport and allocates door number and time slot. Trucks without a valid slot, early, late or at the wrong door wait in the marked driver waiting area until reassigned. Shift supervisors and operators do not change door allocations on their own.

6. Each of the 8 dock doors at 1.2 m dock height has its own leveller, seal, traffic light and chock point. Trailers reverse to the assigned leveller, are chocked and secured, and doors remain closed when no trailer is docked. Levellers are operated only by trained operators and only when the assigned trailer is confirmed on the leveller.

7. Drivers never enter the hall. During docking they remain in the cab or, if required to leave the cab, remain in the marked waiting area and the marked dock-side pedestrian bay. Drivers never enter Zone A, Zone D or any storage aisle. Visitors move only on the 1.2 m walkways under escort and remain in assigned areas.

8. Internal movement uses the fixed aisle system. Main transport aisles of 4.0 m carry forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks between zones and docks. Rack storage aisles in Zone B of 3.0 m serve placement and retrieval only. Aisles are kept clear at all times and are never used for staging. Pedestrians use only the 1.2 m walkways physically separated by yellow barriers and cross only on marked crossings.

9. Speed limits protect every zone interface and are enforced. The limit is 8 km/h inside the building and 15 km/h in the yard on the one-way circulation. Wherever people and trucks meet — marked pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps — the limit is 5 km/h. Limits are signposted at the gate, hall entrances and each shared area.

10. Safe discipline closes the layout. Everyone on the warehouse floor wears a high-visibility vest and class S3 safety footwear with no exceptions, forklift operators wear seat belts when moving, and powered equipment slows to 5 km/h at crossings, walkway openings and dock entries, giving way to pedestrians. Snow, ice, spills, debris and damage to doors, levellers, barriers or markings are reported to the shift supervisor and maintenance technician the same shift, and open faults are carried into the PR-15 handover.

title: Racking and Stacking Limits
text:
### hs.ch03.s1 Racking and Stacking Limits

1. Bulk storage in Zone B of 2,200 m2 uses high-bay pallet racking with 2,400 pallet positions under PR-08. Racking is the only reserve storage above floor level on site. No pallet is placed in racking without a WMS location, a scan-verified pallet licence plate, and a booking that respects the site-wide limit of 800 kg per pallet including load.

2. Each rack bay carries at most 2,700 kg in total, without exception. At full 800 kg per pallet this means no bay holds more than three full-weight pallets. The WMS blocks any fourth placement that would exceed the bay limit. Operators verify bay load plates before placement, never force oversize, overhanging or overweight pallets into beams, and escalate any system proposal that appears to overload a bay to the shift supervisor and stock controllers.

3. Free block-stacking outside racking is permitted only in marked stack positions in Zone B. Stacks are limited to 3 pallets high and 4.0 m total height including pallets, whichever is reached first. Block stacks stand squarely, fully supported on the base, clear of the 4.0 m main transport aisles, the 3.0 m rack storage aisles, the 1.2 m walkways with yellow barriers, dock approaches, sprinkler clearance and marked fire and evacuation routes.

4. Only authorised truck types work the racking under PR-10. The 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t work placement and retrieval inside the 3.0 m rack aisles. The 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t handle horizontal transport to the aisle ends and block-stack placement. No person drives either type without warehouse-manager authorisation and without the documented check before first use each day.

5. Every placement and retrieval is scan-confirmed at the location. The operator scans pallet licence and location label, confirms article, quantity, batch and expiry, places pallets squarely with weight evenly distributed, beams fully engaged and labels facing the aisle, and reports any occupied, damaged, mislabelled or system-mismatched location before placing elsewhere. Leaning pallets, collapsed loads and leaking units are not racked and go to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09.

6. Racking stays in use only with a documented safety inspection every month. The maintenance technician inspects uprights, beams, bracing, base plates, beam locks, floor fixings and load plates across Zone B, plus face and flow-rack frames in Zone C and racking in Zones E and F. The result is recorded with date, area, findings and signature, and filed for audit.

7. Damage found at any time stops work in that aisle. Impact by any truck, falling load, leaning stack, damaged beam or upright, missing lock or plate, or blocked sprinkler is coned off at once, reported the same shift to the shift supervisor in charge and the maintenance technician, and entered in the incident report and repair log with date, equipment, fault and action. The bay or aisle stays out of use until repaired, tested and released by the technician.

8. Storage work follows the fixed traffic and PPE system. Everyone on the floor wears a high-visibility vest and class S3 safety footwear with no exceptions, forklift operators wear seat belts whenever the truck is moving, and powered equipment travels at 8 km/h inside the hall and 5 km/h at crossings, marked pedestrian zones and dock ramps. Pedestrians use only the 1.2 m walkways and marked crossings and never enter a 3.0 m rack aisle while a reach truck is operating inside.

9. Overloads, over-height stacks and damaged racking are safety breaches. They are reported at once, reviewed by the shift supervisor before the next shift starts work, and carried into the PR-15 handover with tag-outs, blocked locations and the due date of the next monthly inspection. Overloaded bays and stacks above 3 pallets or 4.0 m are unloaded immediately on supervisor instruction.

title: Hazmat Storage Limits
text:
### hs.ch03.s2 Hazmat Storage Limits

1. The ventilated hazmat cage in Zone F services and control is the only place hazmat may sit under PR-13. The cage is a separate, locked, ventilated enclosure of 60 m2 within the 600 m2 Zone F, marked, signed and recorded on the site plan. No other zone, aisle, dock, walkway or staging lane is used for hazmat storage at any time.

2. Permitted packed hazmat for regular clients is stored only inside the cage, never in Zone A, B, C, D or E, never in general quarantine, and never on the 4.0 m main transport aisles, the 3.0 m rack storage aisles, dock ramps, staging lanes or the 1.2 m walkways with yellow barriers. Any hazmat pallet found outside the cage is secured, reported at once to the shift supervisor in charge, and moved there immediately or handled as a quarantine case the same shift.

3. The cage holds at most 4,000 kg at a time, without exception. With the site-wide limit of 800 kg per pallet including load, this means at most 5 full-weight pallets in the cage. Weight and pallet count are counted together: lighter pallets do not permit a sixth pallet where weight allows it to exceed safe segregation, and the 5-pallet ceiling applies to full-weight stock as the absolute maximum.

4. The WMS enforces the cage limit before any booking or move. The system blocks any receipt, put-away or transfer that would exceed 4,000 kg in the cage, and inbound operators do not book hazmat in Zone A without confirmed available cage capacity. Open cage quantity in kilograms and pallets is verified each shift by the shift team and carried into the PR-15 handover as a fixed line.

5. Only booked hazmat enters the cage under PR-02 and PR-13. Forklift operators collect pallets in Zone A only after the inbound operator has posted the system receipt with hazard data, fixed the scan-verified WMS pallet licence plate with hazard labels readable, and released the pallet for the cage. Pallets without a verified label, with missing hazard labels, safety data, batch or expiry, or with unresolved document discrepancies stay in Zone A and are never moved to Zone F.

6. Hazmat moves go direct and segregated without staging. On release pallets travel directly from Zone A to the cage clear of main aisles and pedestrian walkways, with powered trucks at 8 km/h inside the hall and 5 km/h at crossings, marked pedestrian zones and dock ramps. The operator scans pallet and cage location on placement, places pallets squarely and fully supported with hazard labels facing the aisle, and keeps incompatible goods separated in the marked bays.

7. Storage conditions in the cage are maintained continuously. Ventilation runs at all times, including nights, shift changeovers at 06:00, 14:00 and 22:00, and any approved Saturday morning overtime when the hall is otherwise closed and locked. Doors are kept closed except for the put-away, issue or check in progress and are confirmed self-closing after each pass. Lighting, ventilation, door seals, signage, fire separation and spill kits are checked each shift.

8. Damaged, leaking or suspect hazmat never remains in the cage as available stock. Spill, leak, odour, vapour, damaged packaging or missing label stops work at once, triggers the PR-13 spill response under the shift supervisor, and the goods go to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09 as system-blocked stock.
