Used absorbents and contaminated packaging are bagged, labelled and held in quarantine for decision.

9. Every receipt, cage quantity, check, fault and quarantine move is recorded and handed over. The shift file, quarantine record and maintenance log hold time, quantities, names and supervisor review, with any fault reported the same shift to the shift supervisor and maintenance technician. Open cage quantity, blocked quarantine, tag-outs and outstanding repairs are carried into the PR-15 handover, and exceeding 4,000 kg or storing hazmat outside the cage is a safety breach reviewed before the next shift starts work.

title: Spills, Quarantine and Damaged Goods
text:
### hs.ch03.s3 Spills, Quarantine and Damaged Goods

1. Any pallet, carton or unit that is crushed, collapsed, leaking, contaminated, mislabelled, past expiry, thaw-suspect or temperature-abused is treated as damaged under PR-09. It is never racked, picked, packed, staged in Zone D or loaded as available stock. The finder stops work on that unit, secures the immediate area, and reports at once to the shift supervisor in charge.

2. Damaged goods go to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found, without exception. Inbound operators, pickers, forklift operators, stock controllers and returns staff move the goods the same shift to the quarantine area, respecting the site-wide limit of 800 kg per pallet including load. Quarantined pallets are never re-cooled, re-racked in Zone B or Zone E, picked for orders or dispatched before a decision.

3. Every quarantine move is labelled and recorded at the point of finding. The label states date, zone and location found, door and carrier or order reference where applicable, article, quantity, batch and expiry, and fault description. The move is entered the same day in the quarantine record with time, name and supervisor notified, and scanned as system-blocked stock on the shared handheld scanners.

4. Quarantined quantities stay system-blocked under stock-controller control. The two stock controllers hold the block so damaged stock is not available to promise, not offered to replenishment for Zone C, and not released to Zone B, E or D. No adjustment to available stock is posted without a second count under PR-08, and no quarantined unit leaves Zone F before the final disposition is approved.

5. Spills, leaks, odours, vapours and broken packaging stop work in the affected area at once. The shift supervisor takes charge of the floor, stops adjacent truck and dock work, cordons the area, and triggers the PR-13 spill response for hazmat. People are kept upwind and clear, pedestrians use only the 1.2 m walkways with yellow barriers, and powered equipment observes 8 km/h inside and 5 km/h at crossings, marked pedestrian zones and dock ramps.

6. Spill response follows containment, protection and quarantine in sequence. Trained staff wear gloves, eye protection and task spill PPE in addition to high-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear, use only the cage spill kit and absorbents, contain liquid to prevent entry to drains and Zone E, ventilate where safe, and move damaged goods to quarantine in Zone F the same day. Spilt goods are never re-racked, picked or dispatched. Used absorbents and contaminated packaging are bagged, labelled and held in quarantine for decision.

7. Returns and packing staff inspect quarantined units and propose disposition. After inspection of every unit for condition, packaging, labelling, batch and expiry, and for cold-chain goods temperature evidence between +2 °C and +8 °C, they propose one outcome per line: restock as compliant stock, rework at the value-added packing workstations, or scrap. The proposal is recorded in the WMS and the shift file. No unit leaves quarantine on the proposer's authority alone.

8. Approval follows the fixed value limit. The shift supervisor in charge approves the final disposition and damaged-goods write-offs up to and including 500 EUR, and releases only passed, fully labelled stock with a WMS licence for put-away. Any case needing write-off above 500 EUR is secured, documented and passed to the warehouse manager the same day. No goods are scrapped, removed or written off above that threshold without that signature. Splitting one case to stay below the threshold is not permitted.

9. All quarantine bookings, spill actions, inspections in progress, dispositions approved and pending, write-offs passed to the manager, and tag-outs and repairs are recorded in the shift file, quarantine record and maintenance log with date, equipment, fault and action. They are reviewed by the shift supervisor before the next shift starts work and carried into the PR-15 handover. Open decisions are never handed over as complete, and secured areas and stopped work remain secured until review is complete.

title: Incident Reporting
text:
1. Every incident on site is reported under PR-14 and handed over under PR-15. Injury, near-miss, damage to racking, trucks or dock equipment, spill, leak, odour or vapour, cold-chain alarm or excursion, fire, evacuation, and any breach of speed, walkway, PPE, authorisation, dock or cage rules is an incident and is reported at once to the shift supervisor in charge.

2. Reporting is immediate and verbal first. The finder stops work on the affected unit, secures the immediate area without creating further risk, keeps people clear and upwind where vapour or spill is involved, and tells the shift supervisor on duty without delay. Powered trucks stop where safe, dock work stops on that door, and pedestrians withdraw to the 1.2 m walkways with yellow barriers.

3. The shift supervisor takes charge of the floor on every incident. The supervisor stops adjacent work where needed, cordons the area, calls the warehouse manager, maintenance technician, stock controllers and dispatcher as required, and calls external services where injury, fire or uncontained spill requires it. No secured area, stopped truck or quarantined pallet is released until the supervisor clears it.

4. Every incident is put in writing before handover. The person involved or the finder completes the incident report with date, time, zone and location, door where applicable, persons and equipment involved, description of what happened, immediate action taken, area secured, and notifications made. Reports are entered in the shift file on that shift and never carried unwritten to the next day.

5. Damaged or suspect goods found through an incident go to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09. They are labelled with date, location, reference and fault, moved respecting the 800 kg pallet limit, and entered in the quarantine record as system-blocked stock. Spills trigger the PR-13 response with the cage spill kit, containment from drains and Zone E, and bagging and labelling of absorbents for decision.

6. Equipment and infrastructure faults are reported as incidents. Defective brakes, steering, belt, horn, light or leak, rack impact, barrier or marking damage, leveller, wrapper or baler fault, and sensor or alarm failure are reported the same shift to the shift supervisor and the maintenance technician. The truck or bay is tagged out, coned off, and logged with date, equipment, fault and action until repaired and tested.

7. The shift supervisor in charge reviews every incident report from the shift before the next shift starts work. The supervisor checks facts, confirms securing and quarantine, countersigns completed reports, and marks incomplete investigations as carried forward with named owner and deadline. Open incidents, secured areas and stopped work are briefed face to face to the incoming supervisor.

8. Serious cases are escalated to the warehouse manager the same day. Any injury requiring treatment beyond first aid, any evacuation, any hazmat spill, any cold-chain excursion outside +2 °C to +8 °C, any rack collapse or bay overload above 2,700 kg, any cage quantity above 4,000 kg, and any write-off case above 500 EUR are notified at once and documented for manager review. Split reporting to avoid escalation is not permitted.

9. All reports, reviews and repairs are filed and carried forward. Incident reports, quarantine entries, cold-log entries and maintenance-log entries are held in the shift file for audit and for the manager's review. Open incidents, tag-outs, blocked locations and outstanding repairs are carried into the PR-15 handover as open, and the next shift starts from the secured position until review and release are complete.

title: Evacuation and Assembly
text:
1. Evacuation is ordered under PR-14 by the shift supervisor in charge. On alarm, fire, injury requiring clearance, spill with vapour, structural damage, power failure affecting safety, or on instruction from the supervisor or the warehouse manager, all work in Zones A to F and at doors 1-8 stops at once and evacuation starts without delay.

2. The shift supervisor takes charge of the floor for the whole evacuation. The supervisor stops trucks and dock work, orders evacuation over the alarm and by voice, prevents re-entry for picks, bookings, loads or counts, and calls the warehouse manager, the maintenance technician and external services as required. No secured area is released until the supervisor clears it.

3. Trucks and installations are left safe only where safe to do so. Operators key off counterbalance forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks where they stand without blocking the 4.0 m main transport aisles, leave dock levellers and the 2 stretch wrappers as they are, and leave without collecting belongings. Doors of Zone E and of the 60 m2 hazmat cage are closed if on the escape path, without delaying exit.

4. Evacuation uses only the marked pedestrian routes. Everyone moves on the 1.2 m walkways with yellow barriers and the marked crossings to the nearest signed emergency exit, clear of moving vehicles and the 3,500 m2 yard manoeuvring area. Shortcuts through the 3.0 m rack storage aisles, blocked aisles, lifts and detours into travel lanes are not permitted.

5. Everyone on site evacuates, without exception. Floor staff, stock controllers, dispatchers, the maintenance technician, supervisors and the manager, drivers from the marked waiting area, dock-side bays and cabs in the manoeuvring area, and escorted visitors leave the hall and yard work areas immediately and follow the yard pedestrian route to the assembly point.

6. The assembly point is by the north fence. All evacuated persons proceed directly there, remain behind the barrier line, and do not leave the point, enter the yard road, approach the hall, or move to meet emergency vehicles. Everyone keeps high-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear on and stays available for roll call.

7. Roll call is completed before anyone re-enters the building. The shift supervisor in charge, with the second supervisor or dispatcher where present, calls the roster, the shift file, the visitor log and the driver list, accounts for every person by name, and records time, names present and absences. Missing persons are reported to the emergency services at once and no search is made by floor staff.

8. Re-entry is permitted only after roll call is complete and the area is released. The supervisor confirms with the warehouse manager and the emergency services that the hall is safe, that Zone E monitoring between +2 °C and +8 °C with alarms, cage ventilation, aisles, racking, levellers, barriers and lighting are checked and intact. No lone re-entry takes place and work resumes only on supervisor instruction.

9. Every evacuation is put in writing before handover. Time of alarm, evacuation time, roll-call result, faults in barriers, markings, lighting, alarms and doors, Zone E and hazmat cage status, and actions taken are entered in the incident report and the shift file under PR-15. The shift supervisor reviews every report before the next shift starts work, and open repairs are passed to the maintenance technician and logged.

title: Checks, Drills and Handover
text:
### hs.ch04.s3 Checks, Drills and Handover

1. Every shift starts with safety checks before productive work begins and ends with a securing check before handover under PR-15. The shift supervisor in charge owns the checks for that shift, assigns who carries them out in Zones A to F and at doors 1-8, and does not release trucks, docks or pick faces until the checks are confirmed. Results are recorded in the shift file and carried into handover.

2. Every powered truck and every hand pallet jack receives a documented check before its first use each day. The assigned authorised operator inspects brakes, steering, lights, horn, seat belt and anchorage, forks, chains, mast, wheels, battery charge and leaks on the 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t and the 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t, and controls, tiller, brakes, wheels and battery on the 8 electric pallet jacks. The 12 hand pallet jacks are checked for wheels, forks and hydraulics. Each check is recorded with date, truck identity, name and signature.

3. Only warehouse-manager-authorised operators drive after checks, and only on the type stated. The supervisor confirms authorisation and completed sheets at the 06:00 and 14:00 starts and at any approved Saturday morning overtime start. Any fault is parked clear of the 4.0 m main aisles, the 3.0 m rack aisles, the 1.2 m walkways with yellow barriers and dock approaches, tagged out, and reported at once to the supervisor and the maintenance technician. Only the technician removes the tag after repair, test and log entry.

4. Docks, aisles, walkways and zones are walked each shift. The team confirms all 8 doors at 1.2 m dock height with levellers, seals, lights and chocks operational, main aisles of 4.0 m and rack aisles of 3.0 m clear, walkways and crossings with yellow barriers intact and lit, speed signs for 8 km/h inside, 15 km/h in the yard and 5 km/h in shared areas readable, and Zone D lanes, Zone F quarantine and the 60 m2 ventilated hazmat cage secured. Any damage, spill, blockage or missing sign is coned off and reported the same shift.

5. Zone E is verified manually each shift. The team reads the independent thermometer, confirms the store held between +2 °C and +8 °C with continuous monitoring and audible alarms active, checks doors self-closing and seals intact, and records time, readings and name in the cold log. Racking stays in use only with the documented monthly safety inspection by the maintenance technician across Zone B with its 2,400 pallet positions and Zones C, E and F, with bay limit 2,700 kg, pallet limit 800 kg and block-stack limit 3 pallets and 4.0 m verified.

6. An evacuation drill is run every quarter under PR-14. The warehouse manager schedules the drill in rotation across morning 06:00-14:00 and afternoon 14:00-22:00 patterns. It covers alarm activation, stopping trucks and dock work, evacuation by walkways and crossings to the assembly point by the north fence, and full roll call before simulated re-entry. Everyone on site takes part, wearing high-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear, with forklift operators wearing seat belts until dismount.

7. Every drill and every real evacuation is put in writing before handover. Time of alarm, evacuation time, roll-call result, faults in barriers, markings, lighting, alarms and doors, and Zone E and cage status are entered in the incident report and shift file. The shift supervisor reviews every report before the next shift starts work, and open repairs are passed to the maintenance technician and logged with date, equipment, fault and action.

8. Every shift ends with a direct, documented handover from the outgoing to the incoming supervisor under PR-15. The record covers work in progress by zone, dock and transport status under dispatcher control, staffing and equipment availability with tag-outs, cycle counts with second counts outstanding, quarantine and cage quantity up to 4,000 kg, cold-log status, and all incidents with securing and notifications. No adjustment is handed over as complete without its second count and no stocktake as closed without manager sign-off.

9. At 14:00 work in progress is carried forward under supervisor ownership, and at 22:00, and at the end of any approved Saturday overtime, the outgoing supervisor additionally confirms aisles clear, doors 1-8 closed with levellers parked, powered equipment keyed off and on charge, quarantine and hazmat cage locked, and Zone E monitoring continuing before the building is locked. Open incidents, tag-outs, blocked locations and drill actions are carried forward as open, and the next shift starts only on checked, authorised equipment after reviewed handover.

title: Warehouse Manager
text:
1. The Warehouse Manager is the single accountable person for the whole Harborwick 3PL site in Port Sellow. The post holder owns operations, safety and inventory accuracy across the 6,000 m2 hall, the six zones A to F, and the 3,500 m2 fenced yard with eight dock doors. Where this manual requires manager approval, no other role may substitute.

2. The Manager sets how the site is run within the fifteen written procedures PR-01 to PR-15. The Manager defines the use of Zone A receiving, Zone B bulk storage, Zone C picking, Zone D dispatch, Zone E cold zone and Zone F services with quarantine and the 60 m2 ventilated hazmat cage, and the one-way use of doors 1-4 inbound and doors 5-8 outbound.

3. The Manager leads the site team of about 38-40 people across two shifts, Monday to Friday 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00, plus Saturday morning overtime in peak season. Direct reports are the two shift supervisors, the two dispatchers, the two stock controllers and the maintenance technician, with forklift operators, inbound operators, pickers, returns and packing staff and floaters reporting through the supervisor in charge of the floor.

4. The Manager delegates day-to-day control of the floor to the shift supervisor on duty, who directs floor staff, sequences zone work and takes charge of incident response. The Manager ensures there is always one named supervisor in charge on every working shift, that handover under PR-15 is direct and documented, and that dispatcher ownership of dock scheduling is respected.

5. The Manager is the final authority for stock integrity. The Manager signs off the annual wall-to-wall stocktake results under PR-08, without which the stocktake is not closed, and ensures cycle counts run every working day on a rotating schedule with no adjustment ever posted without a second count. System stock equal to stock on the rack is the Manager's personal measure.

6. The Manager gives the financial sign-offs for damaged goods under PR-09. The Manager signs off any damaged-goods write-off above 500 EUR, with cases secured, documented and presented the same day they are found. Write-offs up to 500 EUR, final disposition of inspected returns, and review of every incident report are delegated to the shift supervisor, with split write-offs prohibited.

7. Only the Manager approves overtime and driving authority. The Saturday overtime shift, any extension of the 06:00-14:00 or 14:00-22:00 shifts, and any additional hours require prior manager approval. No person drives a counterbalance forklift, reach truck or electric pallet jack independently until the Manager has authorised that person for that equipment type under PR-10, recorded before first use.

8. The Manager owns site safety, capacity and compliance. The Manager enforces the all-electric fleet limits, the 800 kg pallet limit, the 2,700 kg rack-bay limit, the 4,000 kg hazmat-cage limit, the 22,000 kg and 324-pallet shift dispatch ceilings, the 8, 15 and 5 km/h speed system, mandatory high-visibility vests and class S3 footwear, monthly racking inspection, quarterly evacuation drill with roll call at the north fence, and Zone E control between +2 C and +8 C.

title: Shift Supervisor
text:
### roles.ch01.s2 Shift Supervisor

1. The Shift Supervisor runs one shift as the named person in charge of the floor. The two shift supervisors cover the morning shift 06:00-14:00 and the afternoon shift 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday, plus Saturday morning overtime in peak season when approved. There is always one supervisor in charge on every working shift, and the floor is never worked without that supervisor present.

2. The supervisor on duty directs all floor staff during the shift: the inbound operators in Zone A at doors 1-4, the forklift operators on transport, put-away, replenishment and loading, the pickers in Zone C, the dispatch work in Zone D at doors 5-8, and the allocated work in Zone E and Zone F. The supervisor sequences zone work, allocates people and equipment, deploys the floaters to cover absence and peak load, and coordinates timing with the dispatchers, stock controllers and maintenance technician.

3. The supervisor owns the shift checks and start-up. The supervisor assigns the checks in Zones A to F and at doors 1-8, confirms staffing and manager authorisation of every driver under PR-10, confirms documented checks before first use, confirms Zone E verification between +2 °C and +8 °C, confirms aisles, walkways and docks clear, and does not release trucks, docks or pick faces until the checks are confirmed.

4. The supervisor is the first point of response for any incident on the shift. In case of injury, near-miss, damage, spill, temperature alarm, equipment fault or evacuation under PR-13 and PR-14, the supervisor stops work where needed, secures the area, takes charge of the floor, calls the warehouse manager and external services as required, and ensures quarantine moves the same day and the incident report is completed.

5. The supervisor gives the shift-level approvals. The supervisor approves damaged-goods write-offs up to and including 500 EUR under PR-09. Any case above 500 EUR is secured, documented and passed to the warehouse manager the same day, with split write-offs prohibited. The supervisor does not approve overtime, authorise new forklift operators, or sign off the annual stocktake.

6. The supervisor approves the final disposition of every inspected return under PR-07. Returns and packing staff inspect every unit returned within 14 days and propose restock, rework or scrap, but no unit is restocked, reworked or scrapped until the supervisor has reviewed the inspection, confirmed the system block, and approved the proposal. Only passed, fully labelled stock is released for put-away.

7. The supervisor reviews every incident report from the shift before the next shift starts work. The supervisor checks facts, confirms securing and quarantine, countersigns completed reports, and marks incomplete investigations as carried forward with owner and deadline. Serious cases — injury, evacuation, hazmat spill, cold-chain excursion, rack overload or cage breach — are notified to the manager the same day.

8. The supervisor hands over directly to the next supervisor under PR-15. The face-to-face handover with signed record covers work in progress by zone, dock and transport status under dispatcher control, staffing and equipment with tag-outs, cycle counts with second counts outstanding, quarantine and hazmat-cage quantity up to 4,000 kg, cold-log status, and all incidents. At 22:00 the supervisor additionally confirms the site secured, equipment keyed off and on charge, and Zone E monitoring continuing.

9. The supervisor enforces floor discipline throughout the shift. Mandatory high-visibility vests and class S3 footwear, seat belts on moving trucks, the 8 km/h hall, 15 km/h yard and 5 km/h shared-area limits, the 1.2 m walkways with yellow barriers, the 1,000 kg pallet limit, the 2,700 kg bay limit and the block-stack limits are enforced without exception. The supervisor does not change dispatcher door allocations and refers unslotted carriers to the waiting area.

title: Dispatcher
text:
1. The Dispatcher owns dock scheduling and outbound release for the whole site. The two dispatchers cover transport booking and door control from the office annex across the morning shift 06:00-14:00 and the afternoon shift 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday, plus approved Saturday morning overtime. Every carrier movement at doors 1-4 inbound and doors 5-8 outbound runs on a dispatcher allocation.

2. The dispatcher books all transport in advance and assigns every carrier a numbered door and a fixed time slot. Inbound slots are allocated to doors 1-4 opening into Zone A and outbound slots to doors 5-8 served from Zone D, sequenced against Zone A inspection capacity, Zone D staging lanes and shift hours. No other role promises a door or slot, and supervisors and operators do not change allocations.

3. The dispatcher controls arrival and waiting. The dispatcher communicates door and slot to the carrier before departure for Port Sellow, confirms identity at the controlled gate, directs trucks to the assigned door when called or to the marked waiting area, and reassigns trucks that are early, late, unslotted or at the wrong door. Drivers remain in the cab or in the marked waiting area and dock-side bay and never enter the hall.

4. The dispatcher enforces the document-first and booking-before-move rules through scheduling. Inbound trailers stay chocked on doors 1-4 without unloading until inbound operators have checked documents under PR-01, and nothing leaves Zone A for Zone B, E or F until booking is complete. The dispatcher log holds door, slot, carrier, arrival and departure times and reassignments and feeds the PR-15 handover.

5. The dispatcher releases every outbound load from Zone D under PR-06. Release is given only for wrapped, labelled and system-verified pallets staged in the marked lane for the assigned door, with client, order, destination, quantity and pallet identity confirmed on the WMS. No pallet is added, removed or restaged after release without a new dispatcher instruction.

6. The dispatcher plans every load within the fixed capacity ceilings. A pallet may weigh at most 800 kg; the curtain-side trailer carries at most 22,000 kg on 33 floor positions, which means 27 full-weight pallets maximum; the delivery van carries at most 1,200 kg on 6 positions, which means one full-weight pallet. Anything heavier than the van limit goes by trailer.

7. The dispatcher caps bookings at the per-door and per-shift throughput. Each of the 4 outbound doors 5-8 handles at most 3 trailer loads per shift, giving 12 trailer loads per shift site-wide and 324 full-weight pallets per shift as the most that can be promised. Slots beyond 12 departures per shift are not booked, and Zone C completion, wrapping on the 2 stretch wrappers and Zone D staging are sequenced to that ceiling.

8. The dispatcher closes every departure and hands over the position. The dispatcher confirms trailer and van identity, fits and records the seal number, posts despatch in the WMS with door, carrier, time and seal, authorises departure, and carries open loads, delayed carriers, weight or position exceptions and seal records into the PR-15 handover. Trailers docked across the 14:00 or 22:00 changeover stay on their door and slot under dispatcher control until unloading or loading is complete.

title: Inbound Operators
text:
### roles.ch02.s1 Inbound Operators

1. The Inbound Operators own receiving work in Zone A. The six inbound operators cover unloading, counting, inspection and system booking at inbound docks 1-4 across the morning shift 06:00-14:00 and the afternoon shift 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday, plus approved Saturday morning overtime. They work under the direction of the shift supervisor in charge of the floor and to dispatcher-assigned doors and time slots.

2. The operators apply the document-first rule without exception under PR-01. No pallet, carton or unit is moved off the trailer and no unloading equipment is positioned until delivery documents have been presented at the door and checked against dispatcher slot, purchase order, client booking, article numbers, quantities, batch and expiry, and seal and transport condition. Unchecked goods never leave the trailer.

3. On a passed document check the operators unload assigned trailers inside the 800 m2 Zone A. Trailers remain chocked and secured on their 1.2 m leveller with doors open only while docked. Goods are placed into the marked unloading lanes and inspection stations for that door, clear of the 4.0 m main aisles, the 1.2 m walkways with yellow barriers and dock approaches. Forklift support is called only from warehouse-manager-authorised operators after the documented check before first use.

4. Every delivery is counted and inspected at the station before booking. The operators count pallets, cartons and units by delivery note, verify article, quantity, batch and expiry, and check packaging integrity, labelling, damage, leakage, contamination and temperature evidence at the inspection tables. Only inspected goods are presented for booking; uninspected goods are not booked and not put away.

5. The operators perform system booking at the Zone A booking points on the shared WMS scanners. The receipt is posted against purchase order and slot, each pallet receives a licence plate with article, quantity, batch, expiry, receipt date and reference, and the label is fixed and scan-verified. The WMS destination — Zone B bulk, Zone E cold zone, the 60 m2 hazmat cage or Zone F services — is accepted or escalated, respecting the 800 kg pallet limit, the 2,700 kg bay limit and the 4,000 kg cage limit.

6. Release to put-away is a separate confirmation after booking. The operators stage only labelled, scan-readable pallets clear of aisles and walkways, record quantities and destinations in the receiving log, and release pallets for collection. Only released pallets are scanned out of Zone A by forklift operators. Shortages, overages, wrong articles and document failures stay in Zone A marked apart, are escalated the same shift to the supervisor and dispatcher, and are never booked as complete.

7. The operators segregate special and damaged goods at inspection. Cold-chain pallets with +2 °C to +8 °C evidence are booked and moved first by the closed route, hazmat is booked only with cage capacity and moved direct to the cage, and any damaged, leaking or suspect goods go to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found under PR-09, labelled and entered in the quarantine record. Nothing moves past Zone A until paperwork is checked and booking is complete.

8. The operators keep Zone A clear, safe and handed over. Everyone wears high-visibility vests and class S3 footwear, powered equipment observes 8 km/h inside and 5 km/h at crossings and ramps, and spills and debris are cleared before work continues. Receiving log entries, open receipts, unreleased pallets and delayed trailers are recorded in the shift file and carried into the PR-15 handover, with trucks across the 14:00 or 22:00 changeover staying on door and slot under dispatcher control.

title: Forklift Operators
text:
### roles.ch02.s2 Forklift Operators

1. The Forklift Operators provide all powered transport between Zones A to F and the docks. The eight forklift operators cover mornings 06:00-14:00 and afternoons 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday, plus approved Saturday morning overtime. They work under the direction of the shift supervisor in charge of the floor and move only released, booked or tasked pallets to dispatcher-assigned doors and WMS locations.

2. The operators drive the all-electric fleet within fixed types and roles. The 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t handle unloading support in Zone A, horizontal transport to Zone B aisle ends, block-stack placement, replenishment transport to Zone C and loading at outbound doors 5-8. The 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t work only in the high-bay racking in Zone B with its 2,400 pallet positions. The 8 electric pallet jacks cover dock lanes and short transfers. The 12 hand pallet jacks are used for small moves at lanes and packing positions.

3. No operator drives independently until authorised by the warehouse manager under PR-10. Authorisation is separate for counterbalance forklift, reach truck and electric pallet jack, is recorded with name, type and date before first use, and is checked by the supervisor at every shift start. No licence, no truck. An operator uses only the type he is authorised for and never hands a truck to an unauthorised person.

4. Every truck gets a documented check before its first use each day. The assigned operator inspects brakes, steering, lights, horn, seat belt and anchorage, forks, chains, mast, wheels, battery charge and leaks on forklifts and reach trucks, and controls, tiller, brakes, wheels and battery on electric pallet jacks. The result is recorded with date, truck identity, name and signature. A truck without a completed sheet is treated as unchecked and is not released.

5. Any fault stops the truck immediately. The operator parks clear of the 4.0 m main aisles, the 3.0 m rack storage aisles, the 1.2 m walkways with yellow barriers and dock approaches, keys off, tags out, and reports at once to the shift supervisor and the maintenance technician. A defective belt, brake, steering, horn, light or leak is a tag-out fault. Only the maintenance technician removes the tag after repair, test and log entry.

6. The operators observe the fixed aisle, speed and load system on every move. Powered travel uses only the 4.0 m main aisles at 8 km/h inside the hall, with 3.0 m rack aisles entered only for placement and retrieval. The yard limit is 15 km/h, and marked pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps at the 1.2 m dock height are 5 km/h. Operators slow to 5 km/h at every crossing and walkway opening, sound the horn before blind corners, rack entry and dock entry, keep loads low and tilted back, and give way to pedestrians.

7. The operators respect site capacity on every placement. A pallet, load included, may weigh at most 800 kg, each rack bay carries at most 2,700 kg so no bay holds more than three full-weight pallets, and free block-stacking is limited to 3 pallets high and 4.0 m in marked positions. Every put-away, replenishment and loading is scan-confirmed on the shared WMS scanners at pallet and location. Damaged pallets, collapsed loads and system mismatches are not racked and go to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09.

8. The operators work to control points and hand over the position. They collect in Zone A only after booking and release, retrieve in Zone B and Zone E only on WMS task, place only wrapped, labelled pallets in Zone D lanes for doors 5-8, and load only after dispatcher release under PR-06. Everyone wears high-visibility vests and class S3 footwear, with seat belts fastened whenever the truck is moving. Checks, tag-outs, blocked locations and rack damage are recorded in the shift file and carried into the PR-15 handover.

title: Pickers
text:
### roles.ch02.s3 Pickers

1. The Pickers own order fulfilment in Zone C. The ten pickers cover the ground-level pick faces and flow racks in Zone C of 1,200 m2 across the morning shift 06:00-14:00 and the afternoon shift 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday, plus approved Saturday morning overtime. They work under the direction of the shift supervisor in charge of the floor and start work only on faces replenished from bulk before the picking shift.

2. Picking runs only on WMS scanner tasks under PR-04. Each task states article, quantity, batch and expiry, pick-face location and Zone D destination, released from open customer orders. Pickers collect only the tasked quantity from the tasked face. Picking from reserve racking, from Zone A, from Zone D staging, from quarantine or from the 60 m2 hazmat cage is not permitted, and picking on memory, paper or judgement is not permitted.

3. Pickers work on the 20 shared handheld WMS scanners signed out and tested at shift start. They log in, accept one task at a time, scan the face location label then scan each article or carton picked. The scanner confirms article, batch and expiry and blocks wrong picks, short faces and system-blocked stock. Any scanner, label or system mismatch stops that pick until the shift supervisor and stock controllers resolve it.

4. Every picked item is scan-verified before it is packed. The picker scans item against task, checks count, condition and date, keeps older batch and earlier expiry to the front under rotation, and builds the order pallet or tote squarely without crushing, overhang or mixed batches. Unverified, damaged, leaking or suspect units are never packed for the order and go to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found under PR-09.

5. Pickers pack, label and transfer completed units to dispatch under PR-05. They confirm task-complete in the WMS, fix the order label with client, order, destination and pallet identity, scan-verify readability, and move labelled pallets with the 12 hand pallet jacks or call a warehouse-manager-authorised forklift operator for powered moves. Only labelled, system-confirmed units leave Zone C for Zone D, built within the 800 kg limit per pallet including load.

6. Shortages, empty faces, wrong stock and damage stop the task at the face. The picker leaves the face marked, records short, damaged or mislocated quantity in the scanner, and reports at once to the shift supervisor and stock controllers. The face is not topped up by the picker and no substitution is made. Replenishment is re-tasked from Zone B or Zone E, and no adjustment is posted without a second count under PR-08.

7. Pickers keep cold-chain and hazmat segregation on every order. Cold orders are picked only from released, in-temperature faces between +2 °C and +8 °C with Zone E doors kept shut, and move first by the closed route without ambient staging. Hazmat is never picked to general faces and stays only in the ventilated cage up to 4,000 kg. Thaw-suspect, leaking or temperature-abused units are labelled with date, face, reference and fault and entered in the quarantine record.

8. Pickers keep faces clear, safe and handed over. Everyone wears high-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear, powered equipment observes 8 km/h inside the hall and 5 km/h at crossings, pedestrian zones and dock ramps, and pedestrians use only the 1.2 m walkways with yellow barriers, crossing only on marked crossings. Open scanner tasks, short faces, quarantine moves, face or rack damage and scanner faults are recorded in the shift file and carried into the PR-15 handover.

title: Stock Controllers
text:
1. The Stock Controllers own inventory accuracy day to day across the whole site. The two stock controllers cover Zone B bulk storage with its 2,400 pallet positions, Zone C pick faces, Zone E cold zone, Zone F services with quarantine and the 60 m2 ventilated hazmat cage, and open pallets in Zone A and Zone D. They work across the morning shift 06:00-14:00 and the afternoon shift 14:00-22:00 to support both shifts, under the warehouse manager with timing coordinated with the shift supervisor in charge.

2. The controllers run cycle counts every working day on a rotating zone schedule under PR-08. The daily plan states zone, aisle, rack positions or faces, articles and start time, sequenced to avoid blocking replenishment before the picking shift, put-away from Zone A and loading at doors 5-8. No working day passes without planned counts, plus approved Saturday morning overtime when ordered.

3. Counting runs only on WMS task on the 20 shared handheld scanners. The controller scans location label then pallet licence plate, confirms article, quantity, batch and expiry, and posts the first-count result without adjusting stock. Pallets under count are not moved, re-labelled or put away, and forklift operators hold placement and retrieval in that aisle until the count is released.

4. No adjustment is ever posted without a second count. Every difference between first count and system triggers a mandatory independent recount by a stock controller, with re-scan of location and pallet, re-check of batch and expiry, and check of adjacent locations, pick faces and staging lanes for misplacement. If second count differs from first, a third check with the shift supervisor decides the correct quantity before posting.

5. The controllers post adjustments only after recount in the WMS under PR-08. Each posting records date, time, zone and location, article and quantities before and after, first- and second-count names and reason for misplacement, damage, expiry or system error. Open differences, unrecounted first counts and held adjustments are carried into the PR-15 handover as open and are never handed over as complete.

6. The controllers hold system blocks for quarantine and special stock. Damaged, leaking, suspect and temperature-abused goods moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found stay blocked and are not available to promise or offered to Zone C replenishment until final disposition is approved. Cold-chain stock between +2 °C and +8 °C stays in Zone E unless quarantined, and hazmat stays only in the cage within the 4,000 kg limit and is counted in place.

7. The controllers prepare and run the annual wall-to-wall stocktake under PR-08 for manager sign-off. They tidy and label locations with the supervisors, close or carry forward open cycle-count differences, freeze the WMS with the dispatcher closing doors 1-4 and 5-8, count in paired teams on stocktake task without adjusting, recount every difference, and present reconciled results with quarantine moves and unresolved items. Without the manager's signature the stocktake is not closed.

8. The controllers verify cold-zone and racking controls through the count routine. They include Zone E in daily rotation with no interruption to +2 °C to +8 °C monitoring, alarms and manual verification each shift under PR-12, respect the 800 kg pallet limit and the 2,700 kg bay limit on every location, report blocked locations, mislabelled cartons and rack damage the same shift to the supervisor and maintenance technician, and record counts, recounts, adjustments, quarantine bookings and faults in the cycle-count log and shift file for PR-15 handover.

title: Returns and Packing Staff
text:
### roles.ch03.s2 Returns and Packing Staff

1. The Returns and Packing Staff own returns inspection, value-added packing and quarantine handling in Zone F. The four staff cover the returns-inspection area, the value-added packing workstations and the quarantine area in Zone F services and control of 600 m2 across the morning shift 06:00-14:00 and the afternoon shift 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday, plus approved Saturday morning overtime. They work under the direction of the shift supervisor in charge of the floor and in coordination with the stock controllers.

2. Returns are handled only in Zone F under PR-07. All customer returns for the twenty regular clients arrive via doors 1-4 inbound and are moved directly to Zone F without inspection in Zone A, storage in Zone B, picking in Zone C or staging in Zone D. Returns are accepted only within 14 days of delivery, checked against delivery date, client, order and authorisation at receipt, with late or unauthorised returns held apart and escalated to the supervisor and dispatcher.

3. Every returned unit is inspected individually on WMS task. The staff scan return reference, article and location on the 20 shared handheld scanners, open, count and check condition, packaging integrity, labelling, batch and expiry, leakage, contamination and, for cold-chain goods, temperature evidence between +2 °C and +8 °C. No sampling is permitted. Received quantities stay system-blocked and are not available to promise during inspection, with the block held by the stock controllers.

4. After inspection of every unit the staff propose one disposition per line: restock to Zone B, C or E, rework at the packing workstations, or scrap via quarantine. The proposal states quantities, batch, expiry, condition and reason and is recorded in the WMS and the shift file. No unit leaves the inspection area on the proposer's authority alone, and no returned unit is restocked, reworked or scrapped until the shift supervisor approves the final disposition.

5. Damaged, leaking, suspect and temperature-abused goods go to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found under PR-09. The staff label each move with date, reference, location and fault, move it the same shift respecting the 800 kg limit per pallet including load, and enter it in the quarantine record as blocked stock. Quarantined units are never re-cooled, re-racked, picked or dispatched before a decision, and hazmat returns stay only in the 60 m2 ventilated cage within the 4,000 kg limit.

6. Value-added packing is performed only at the Zone F workstations under PR-07 and PR-09. The staff carry out rework, repacking, relabelling and kitting only after supervisor approval, on WMS rework task stating source reference, article, quantity and destination. Finished cartons and pallets receive a WMS licence with article, quantity, batch, expiry and reference, fixed squarely and scan-verified. Only released, labelled pallets are collected by forklift operators, respecting the 2,700 kg rack-bay limit and the closed route for Zone E.

7. Packing waste is handled at source. Only clean, dry cardboard is fed to the single cardboard baler, with strapping, film, wood and general waste kept out. Workstations stand set back behind barriers clear of the 4.0 m main aisles and the 1.2 m walkways with yellow barriers, with one job per table, compliant output separated from quarantined input, and waste removed to its marks without blocking sprinklers or evacuation routes.

8. The staff keep Zone F clear, safe and handed over. Everyone wears high-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear, powered equipment observes 8 km/h inside the hall and 5 km/h at crossings, pedestrian zones and dock ramps, and pedestrians use only walkways and marked crossings. Cases needing write-off above 500 EUR are secured for warehouse manager sign-off, with split write-offs prohibited. Open returns, rework in progress, quarantine bookings, baler faults and pending dispositions are recorded in the shift file and carried into the PR-15 handover.

title: Maintenance Technician
text:
### roles.ch03.s3 Maintenance Technician

1. The Maintenance Technician owns the serviceability of all trucks, racking and dock equipment on site. The single technician covers the morning shift 06:00-14:00 and the afternoon shift 14:00-22:00 in coordination with the shift supervisor in charge, Monday to Friday, plus approved Saturday morning overtime, under the warehouse manager. All planned checks, breakdown repairs and safety inspections pass through this role.

2. The technician maintains the all-electric MHE fleet under PR-10. The 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t, the 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t for the high bays in Zone B, the 8 electric pallet jacks and the 12 hand pallet jacks are inspected, serviced and repaired only by the technician. The documented check before first use each day is carried out by the authorised operator, and any fault reported is parked clear of the 4.0 m main aisles, the 3.0 m rack aisles and dock approaches, tagged out and repaired, tested and logged before release.

3. The technician maintains fixed dock and packing plant under PR-06. Each of the 8 dock doors at 1.2 m dock height with its leveller, seal, traffic light and chock point, the 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers in Zone D dispatch of 900 m2, and the single cardboard baler are serviced on plan and on breakdown. A faulty leveller, wrapper, guard or interlock takes that door or machine out of service, coned off, until repaired and logged. Only the technician removes a tag after repair and test.

4. Racking stays in use only with a documented safety inspection every month under PR-08. The technician inspects all high-bay racking in Zone B with its 2,400 pallet positions, uprights, beams, bracing, base plates, beam locks, floor fixings and bay load plates, plus face and flow-rack frames in Zone C of 1,200 m2 and racking in Zone E and Zone F. The result is recorded with date, area, findings and signature. Each bay is verified at most 2,700 kg total, pallets at most 800 kg including load, and block-stacking at 3 pallets high and 4.0 m in marked positions.

5. Damage found at any time is acted on the same shift. Impact by any truck, leaning pallet, collapsed load, missing lock or plate, barrier or marking damage, or blocked sprinklers is coned off with the shift supervisor, stops work in that bay or aisle, and is entered in the incident report and the repair log with date, equipment, fault and action. The bay or aisle stays out of use until the technician has repaired, tested and released it.

6. The technician supports cold-chain, hazmat and building services under PR-12 and PR-13. Refrigeration, continuous monitoring and audible alarms in Zone E held between +2 C and +8 C, ventilation, seals, lighting, signage, fire separation and spill kits in the 60 m2 ventilated hazmat cage in Zone F, walkway yellow barriers, mirrors, lighting and speed signs for 8 km/h inside, 15 km/h in the yard and 5 km/h in shared areas are checked, repaired and logged. Zone E monitoring and cage ventilation remain active when the hall is otherwise closed and locked.

7. The technician supports evacuation readiness and response under PR-14. Alarms, emergency exits, walkway routes to the assembly point by the north fence, dock securing and the keying-off of powered equipment are tested in the quarterly evacuation drill scheduled by the warehouse manager across morning and afternoon patterns. On a real alarm the technician reports to the supervisor in charge, isolates power and plant as instructed, and repairs faults in barriers, lighting, alarms and doors before re-entry after roll call is complete.

8. The technician logs, files and hands over every job. Every repair is logged with date, equipment identity, fault found and action taken in the maintenance log, with check sheets, tag-outs, monthly racking inspections and drill actions recorded in the shift file for audit and manager review. Open faults, tag-outs, blocked bays and outstanding repairs are carried into the PR-15 handover as open. Everyone on the floor wears high-visibility vests and class S3 footwear, with seat belts on moving trucks, and no overtime is worked without prior warehouse manager approval.

title: Inbound Receiving Hours and Intake
text:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. receives inbound goods Monday to Friday within the two operating shifts: morning shift 06:00–14:00 and afternoon shift 14:00–22:00. Inbound unloading, document check, inspection and system booking are performed only inside these windows. No regular receiving is offered outside these hours.

2. In peak season a Saturday morning overtime shift may be added for backlog inbound. Saturday receiving is overtime only, requires prior approval by the warehouse manager, is confirmed to the client in advance for that Saturday only, and does not create a permanent weekend service. Unapproved arrivals on Saturday will not be unloaded.

3. All inbound deliveries arrive only on a dispatcher-assigned door and time slot. The dispatcher books transport with the carrier, allocates one of inbound doors 1–4 and a fixed slot sequenced against Zone A capacity and shift hours, and communicates both before dispatch to Port Sellow. Doors 1–4 open only into Zone A receiving of 800 m2. Doors 5–8 are outbound only and are never used for inbound.

4. Carriers report to the controlled gate with carrier, client, purchase order reference, assigned door and slot time, and transport documents. Trucks without a valid slot, arriving early, late or at the wrong door wait in the marked driver waiting area until the dispatcher reassigns them. Drivers remain in the cab or in the marked waiting area and dock-side bay and never enter the hall. The client ensures its carriers respect slot, door and waiting instructions.

5. We apply a document-first standard to every load without exception. Nothing is unloaded until delivery documents have been presented at the door and checked against dispatcher slot, purchase order and client booking, article numbers, quantities, batch and expiry data where required, and seal and visible transport condition. If documents are missing, incomplete or do not match the booking, unloading does not start and the goods remain on the trailer pending correction.

6. On a passed document check we unload, count and inspect in Zone A before any booking. We count pallets, cartons and units by delivery note and purchase order and inspect packaging integrity, labelling, damage, leakage, contamination and, where applicable, temperature evidence and cold-chain labelling at the inspection stations. Only inspected goods are presented for booking; uninspected goods are never booked and never moved past Zone A.

7. Only inspected goods are booked into the WMS, and only booked goods are released to put-away in Zone B, Zone E or Zone F. Booking is posted against purchase order and slot on handheld scanners immediately after inspection is passed, with article, counted quantity, batch and expiry confirmed. Each booked pallet receives a WMS pallet licence plate, fixed and scan-verified before it leaves Zone A. The client receives intake confirmation only on booked quantities.

8. Shortages, overages, wrong articles, batch or expiry mismatches and visible transport damage stop booking for that line. Passed quantity may be booked as a short receipt where the system permits; the balance stays in Zone A marked apart. Damaged or suspect goods go to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found. We escalate the discrepancy the same shift to the supervisor and dispatcher, record door, carrier, reference, times, counts and inspection result in the receiving log, and do not release the trailer as complete until the case is resolved or formally recorded.

title: Outbound Dispatch Capacity and Cut-Offs
text:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. dispatches outbound goods Monday to Friday within the two operating shifts: morning shift 06:00–14:00 and afternoon shift 14:00–22:00. Staging in Zone D, wrapping, final checks, loading and sealing are performed only inside these windows. No regular dispatch is offered outside these hours.

2. In peak season a Saturday morning overtime shift may be added for pre-staged outbound loads. Saturday dispatch is overtime only, requires prior approval by the warehouse manager, is confirmed to the client in advance for that Saturday only, and does not create a permanent weekend service. Loads not confirmed for that Saturday will not be loaded.

3. All outbound loading uses doors 5–8 only. Doors 5–8 open from Zone D dispatch of 900 m2 with marked staging lanes per door. Doors 1–4 are inbound only and are never used for outbound. Every carrier is assigned a numbered outbound door and a fixed time slot by the dispatcher before arrival, sequenced against staging-lane capacity and shift hours. Trucks without a valid slot, arriving early, late or at the wrong door wait in the marked driver waiting area until reassigned.

4. We commit a fixed per-door throughput of 3 trailer loads per shift. Turnaround per load includes docking at the 1.2 m leveller, check of wrap and labels, scan-loading, sealing and departure. This gives a site-wide commitment of 12 trailer loads per shift across the 4 outbound doors. We do not book slots beyond 12 trailer departures per shift.

5. Trailer capacity governs our per-shift pallet commitment. The standard contracted curtain-side trailer carries at most 22,000 kg on 33 floor positions. A pallet, load included, may weigh at most 800 kg, so weight is reached at 27 full-weight pallets. We plan a maximum of 27 full-weight pallets per trailer; lighter pallets may use more floor positions only while total weight stays at or below 22,000 kg. Floor positions are loaded stably without overhang or mixing of unreleased orders.

6. Per-shift site capacity is therefore 324 full-weight pallets per shift: 12 trailer loads at 27 full-weight pallets each. That is the most we promise a client for one shift. Zone C completion, wrapping on the 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers and Zone D staging are sequenced to that ceiling. The small-drop delivery van is committed separately at most 1,200 kg on 6 positions: one full-weight pallet only, with remaining capacity for light cartons up to the total. Anything heavier, or more than one full-weight pallet, goes by trailer.

7. Only wrapped, labelled and system-released pallets are staged and loaded. Pallets are built within the 800 kg limit, scan-verified against the customer order, labelled with client, order, destination and pallet identity, and wrapped to a stable, fully enclosed load with labels readable. Pallets without a verified label or not on the released load are held apart and never loaded. Cold-chain orders between +2 °C and +8 °C move first by the closed route but count identically toward trailer weight, positions and the 324-pallet total.

8. We apply a release cut-off to every load without exception. The dispatcher releases each load in the WMS only when the lane for the assigned door is complete and verified, confirms trailer identity, and calls the truck from the waiting area. Loading starts only after release, with each pallet scanned out of Zone D. No pallet is added, removed or restaged after release without a new dispatcher instruction, and orders not released by their slot time roll to the next available slot or shift. The load is closed only with open lines resolved, then sealed with seal number recorded, despatch posted with door, carrier, time and seal, and departure authorised. Open loads, delayed carriers and weight or position exceptions are carried into shift handover with door and slot intact.

title: Order Accuracy and Pick-Pack Standard
text:
1. We pick customer orders only in Zone C picking of 1,200 m2 from ground-level pick faces and flow racks. Reserve racking in Zone B, Zone A receiving, Zone D staging, quarantine and the 60 m2 hazmat cage are never used as pick locations. We start picking each shift only on faces replenished before that shift from Zone B bulk storage, and for cold faces from Zone E, so released, system-available stock is in position.

2. Replenishment to the faces runs only on WMS task under PR-03. We generate replenishment from open customer orders and minimum levels, retrieve the tasked source pallet with scan confirmation of pallet licence and location, and place within the marked face quantity without overfilling, crushing or blocking labels, keeping older batch and earlier expiry to the front. We never top up faces on judgement, and overstock remains in bulk.

3. Picking runs only on WMS scanner tasks under PR-04. Each task states article, quantity, batch and expiry where required, pick-face location and Zone D destination. Our pickers accept one task at a time on handheld scanners, scan face location then each article or carton picked, and the system blocks wrong picks, short faces and system-blocked stock. We do not pick on memory, paper or substitution.

4. We apply a scan-verified pack standard to every order line without exception. Every picked item is scan-verified against the task before it is packed, with count, condition, article, batch and expiry checked and rotation maintained. Unverified, short-picked, wrong-batch, damaged, leaking or suspect units are never packed for dispatch and go to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found.

5. Packed units are built, labelled and transferred as completed units under PR-05. We build stable order pallets and cartons without crushing, overhang or mixed batches, within the site-wide limit of 800 kg per pallet including load. Each pallet and carton receives a WMS order label with client, order, destination, article, quantity, batch and expiry where required, and pallet identity, fixed squarely and scan-verified for readability before it leaves the packing position. Units without a verified label never enter Zone D staging and are never wrapped as finished loads.

6. Finished pallets are wrapped and staged only in Zone D dispatch of 900 m2. We wrap on the 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers to a stable, fully enclosed load with base, corners and top secured and labels left readable, and stage only wrapped, labelled and system-confirmed pallets in the marked lane for the assigned outbound door 5-8. Shortages, empty faces, wrong stock and damage stop the task at the face; we record the exception in the scanner, leave the face marked, re-task replenishment from Zone B or Zone E, and never post an adjustment without a second count.

7. Cold-chain and special goods keep full segregation through pick and pack. Cold orders are picked only from released, in-temperature faces between +2 C and +8 C and move first by the closed route to Zone D without ambient staging. Hazmat stays only in the ventilated cage up to 4,000 kg and is never picked to general faces. Damaged, thaw-suspect or temperature-abused units found at pick or pack are labelled with date, face or order, reference and fault and entered in the quarantine record as blocked stock.

8. We measure order accuracy as the share of despatched order lines delivered exactly as ordered: correct article, correct quantity, correct batch and expiry where required, correct label and correct destination, with scan verification closed in the WMS. Short lines, held pallets and quarantine moves are not closed as complete, and no pallet is loaded until the dispatcher releases the load under PR-06. Open tasks, short faces, re-wraps, printer and wrapper faults and quarantine bookings are recorded in the shift file and carried into handover, so the client receives only verified, released and traceable loads.

title: Storage Zones and Capacity Limits
text:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. stores client stock only inside the six fixed zones of the 6,000 m2 hall. General reserve stock sits in Zone B bulk storage of 2,200 m2, active pick stock sits in Zone C picking of 1,200 m2, temperature-sensitive stock sits in Zone E cold zone of 300 m2, and permitted hazmat, quarantine and value-added stock sits in Zone F services of 600 m2. Zone A receiving of 800 m2 and Zone D dispatch of 900 m2 are transit areas only and are never used for storage.

2. Zone B bulk storage provides 2,400 pallet positions in high-bay racking plus marked block-stack positions. Every client pallet booked to Zone B holds a WMS-assigned location with scan-verified licence plate, article, quantity, batch and expiry. We put away only booked goods to a confirmed location and scan-confirm pallet and location on placement, with labels facing the aisle.

3. We apply a site-wide pallet limit of 800 kg per pallet, load included, to all client stock. That figure governs every rack, cage, trailer and handling commitment. No client pallet is accepted, built, racked or staged above 800 kg, and any unit exceeding it is split, repacked or replanned before put-away.

4. Each rack bay in Zone B carries at most 2,700 kg in total without exception. At full 800 kg per pallet this means no bay holds more than three full-weight pallets. Our WMS blocks any fourth placement that would exceed the bay limit, and we verify bay load plates before placement. Overweight, oversize or overhanging pallets are never forced into racking.

5. Free block-stacking outside racking is offered only in marked stack positions in Zone B. Stacks are limited to 3 pallets high and 4.0 m total height including pallets, whichever is reached first. Block stacks stand clear of the 4.0 m main transport aisles, the 3.0 m rack storage aisles, pedestrian walkways, dock approaches, sprinkler clearance and evacuation routes.

6. Zone C holds only released replenishment stock and open customer orders on ground-level pick faces and flow racks, fed from Zone B and for cold faces from Zone E. Overstock remains in bulk and faces are never overfilled. Zone E holds only booked cold-chain goods continuously between +2 °C and +8 °C, with doors kept closed except for the move in progress. No ambient, hazmat, quarantine or packing stock is stored in Zone E.

7. Zone F holds the separate ventilated hazmat cage of 60 m2 and the quarantine area. The cage is the only place hazmat may sit and holds at most 4,000 kg at a time, which means at most 5 full-weight pallets. We do not book hazmat without confirmed cage capacity and the WMS blocks any receipt that would exceed the limit. Quarantine holds damaged and suspect goods after they are found the same day, system-blocked and unavailable to promise until final disposition.

8. Zone capacity, load limits and cage quantity are verified each shift and carried into handover. Overloaded bays, over-height stacks, hazmat outside the cage and goods held outside their assigned zone are treated as non-conformances, unloaded or relocated at once, recorded with location and time, and reported to the client where its stock is affected. Racking remains in use only with a documented safety inspection every month.

title: Cycle Counts and Annual Stocktake
text:
1. We count client stock every working day, Monday to Friday, on a rotating zone schedule under PR-08. Our two stock controllers own the schedule so that Zone B bulk storage with its 2,400 pallet positions, Zone C pick faces, Zone E cold zone, Zone F services including quarantine and the 60 m2 hazmat cage, and open pallets in Zone A and Zone D are all counted in rotation. No working day passes without planned counts.

2. Daily counts are sequenced to protect service. We plan zone, aisle, positions, articles and start time inside the morning shift 06:00–14:00 and afternoon shift 14:00–22:00, avoiding blockage of replenishment before the picking shift, put-away from Zone A and loading at doors 5–8. In peak season counts may extend to approved Saturday morning overtime. The client is not required to attend for daily counts to be valid.

3. Counting runs only on WMS task on handheld scanners. We scan location label then pallet licence plate, confirm article, quantity, batch and expiry where required, and post the first-count result without adjusting stock. Pallets under count are not moved, re-labelled or put away, and placement and retrieval in that aisle are held until the count is released.

4. We commit a recount-before-adjustment standard without exception. Every difference between first count and system quantity triggers a mandatory independent second count by a stock controller, with re-scan of location and pallet, re-check of batch and expiry, and check of adjacent locations, pick faces and staging lanes for misplacement. If second count differs from first, a third check with the shift supervisor decides the correct quantity before posting.

5. Adjustments are posted only after recount and leave a full audit trail. Each posting records date, time, zone and location, article and quantities before and after, first- and second-count names and reason for misplacement, damage, expiry or system error. Open differences, unrecounted first counts and held adjustments are never treated as complete and are carried into shift handover as open.

6. Special stock is counted in place without breaking control. Zone E remains between +2 °C and +8 °C with monitoring, alarms and manual verification each shift during counts, and cold stock stays in Zone E unless quarantined. Hazmat stays only in the cage within the 4,000 kg limit. Damaged, leaking or temperature-abused units found during counts go to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found as system-blocked stock, unavailable to promise until final disposition.

7. We hold a wall-to-wall stocktake once a year as a full shutdown count of all client stock under PR-08. All six zones A to F are counted with no location excluded. The date is set in advance by the warehouse manager and confirmed to the client. Inbound at doors 1–4, outbound at doors 5–8, put-away, replenishment and picking are stopped for the stocktake period, trailers stay on door without unloading or loading, and the WMS is frozen so no receipts, issues, moves or adjustments are posted during the freeze.

8. The annual count is performed in paired teams on WMS stocktake task, scanning location then pallet and confirming article, quantity, batch and expiry. First-count results are posted without adjusting stock and counted pallets are not moved until the area is released. Every difference triggers a mandatory independent recount, and damaged units go to quarantine the same day. Zone E doors stay shut except for the count in progress and hazmat remains in the cage.

9. The annual result is closed only with the warehouse manager's sign-off. We reconcile first and second counts, list confirmed differences, postings proposed, quarantine moves and unresolved items, and present the result for signature. Without that signature the stocktake is not closed and system figures are not taken as verified. On sign-off we post adjustments after second count, record results in the stocktake file, resume normal flow, and restart the daily rotating cycle-count schedule from the signed position to keep system stock equal to stock on the rack.

title: Stock Reporting and Accountability
text:
1. The WMS is the sole system of record for client stock. System quantity equals physical quantity on the rack only after the fixed controls are met: booking only after inspection, put-away only after booking, no adjustment without a second count, quarantine stock held as system-blocked, and the annual result valid only with manager sign-off. No spreadsheet, email or verbal figure overrides the WMS.

2. Day-to-day accuracy is owned by our two stock controllers. They run the daily rotating cycle-count schedule, perform mandatory second counts, post adjustments only after recount with date, time, zone, location, quantities before and after, names and reason, hold system blocks for quarantine in Zone F, and keep the cycle-count log, quarantine record and shift file consistent for handover under PR-15.

3. Site accountability sits with the warehouse manager. The manager owns operations, safety and inventory accuracy across Zones A to F, sets zone use under PR-01 to PR-15, and is the final authority for stock integrity. System stock equal to stock on the rack is the manager's personal measure for all twenty regular clients.

4. We report intake, stock position and exceptions on a fixed cadence. Intake is confirmed only on booked quantities after Zone A inspection, with purchase order, door, carrier, counted quantities and labels issued. Open receipts, short receipts, overages and quarantines are reported the same shift they are found with reference, location and time.

5. Daily progress is reported through the shift file and cycle-count log. Counts completed, second counts outstanding, adjustments posted and held, quarantine bookings, blocked locations, Zone E verification between +2 °C and +8 °C, and hazmat-cage quantity up to 4,000 kg are recorded each shift. Open differences are carried forward as open and are never reported as complete.

6. The annual wall-to-wall stocktake is reported as a reconciled pack for sign-off. We present first and second counts, confirmed differences, postings proposed, quarantine moves, blocked positions and unresolved items. Without the warehouse manager's signature the stocktake is not closed and system figures are not taken as verified. On sign-off we file the result in the stocktake file and restart daily counts from the signed position.

7. Financial and disposition sign-offs follow fixed thresholds. The shift supervisor in charge approves damaged-goods write-offs up to and including 500 EUR, the final disposition of every inspected return, and reviews every incident report from the shift before the next shift starts work. Any write-off above 500 EUR is secured, documented and passed to the warehouse manager the same day, with no scrapping or removal without that signature and no splitting to stay below the threshold.

8. The client receives only verified, traceable figures. Reports state source WMS transaction, count names, verification time and approval given, with blocked quarantine quantities shown separately as unavailable to promise. Where client stock is affected by damage, shortage, rack incident, excursion or cage breach, we record location, time and action taken, hold the position secured until review is complete, and make the audit trail available from the receiving log, cycle-count log, quarantine record and stocktake file.

title: Damaged Goods and Quarantine
text:
1. We treat any pallet, carton or unit that is crushed, collapsed, leaking, contaminated, mislabelled, past expiry, thaw-suspect or temperature-abused as damaged stock. Damaged units are never racked, picked, packed, staged in Zone D or loaded as available stock. On finding, we stop work on that unit, secure the immediate area and report at once to the shift supervisor in charge.

2. We apply a same-day quarantine standard without exception under PR-09. All damaged and suspect goods found in Zones A to F, including inbound inspection, put-away, replenishment, picking, packing, counts and cold-chain checks, are moved the same day they are found to the quarantine area in Zone F services and control of 600 m2. Quarantined pallets respect the site-wide limit of 800 kg per pallet including load and are never re-cooled, re-racked in Zone B or Zone E, picked for orders or dispatched before a decision.

3. Every quarantine move is labelled and recorded at the point of finding. We mark date, zone and location found, door and carrier or order reference where applicable, article, quantity, batch and expiry where required, and fault description, and enter it the same day in the quarantine record with time, name and supervisor notified. The move is scanned as system-blocked stock on handheld scanners so it is unavailable to promise.

4. Quarantined quantities stay system-blocked under stock-controller control. Our two stock controllers hold the block so damaged stock is not offered to replenishment for Zone C, not released to Zone B, E or D, and not shown as available in any client report. No adjustment to available stock is posted without a mandatory independent second count, and no quarantined unit leaves Zone F before final disposition is approved.

5. We inspect every quarantined unit and propose a single outcome per line. Our returns and packing staff check condition, packaging integrity, labelling, batch and expiry, and for cold-chain goods temperature evidence between +2 °C and +8 °C, with no sampling. We propose restock as fully compliant stock, rework at the value-added packing workstations, or scrap, and record quantities, condition and reason in the WMS and shift file. No unit leaves quarantine on the proposer's authority alone.

6. Final disposition follows fixed approval thresholds that protect the client. The shift supervisor in charge approves the disposition and any damaged-goods write-off up to and including 500 EUR, and releases only passed, fully labelled stock with a WMS licence for put-away under PR-02. Cold-chain goods are never re-cooled and re-racked after excursion, and hazmat stays only in the 60 m2 ventilated cage within the 4,000 kg limit. Splitting one case to stay below the threshold is not permitted.

7. Any case needing write-off above 500 EUR is secured, documented and passed to the warehouse manager the same day. No goods in that case are scrapped, removed from stock or written off without the manager's signature. The pallet stays locked in Zone F with its record complete, system block maintained, and audit trail held until sign-off is given and posted.

8. We report quarantine and write-off cases on the day they occur. The client receives reference, location and time found, article and quantities held, fault and photographs where available, proposal made, approval given or pending, and blocked quantity shown separately as unavailable to promise. Open inspections, pending dispositions and cases passed to the manager are carried forward as open in the shift file, quarantine record and handover, and are never reported as closed until approval is posted and the WMS, cycle-count log and stocktake file are aligned.

title: Returns Handling and Disposition
text:
1. We accept customer returns only within 14 days of delivery under PR-07. All returns for our regular clients arrive via inbound doors 1–4 and are moved directly to the returns-inspection area in Zone F services and control of 600 m2. No return is inspected in Zone A, stored in Zone B, picked in Zone C or staged in Zone D before inspection is complete.

2. Returns must be authorised and traceable to the original despatch. On receipt in Zone F we check delivery date against return request, client, order, article and authorisation. Returns outside 14 days, without authorisation, or outside packed consumer goods are held apart as unauthorised and escalated the same shift to the shift supervisor and dispatcher without inspection for stock. The client ensures its customers quote order and delivery reference with every return.

3. We inspect every returned unit individually with no sampling. Our returns and packing staff open, count and check condition, packaging integrity, labelling, batch and expiry where required, leakage, contamination and, for cold-chain goods, temperature evidence between +2 °C and +8 °C. Uninspected units are never restocked, reworked, scrapped or released to any zone.

4. Inspection runs only on WMS task on handheld scanners. We scan return reference, article and location, post received quantity as system-blocked stock, and record inspected quantity by condition. Returned quantities stay blocked and unavailable to promise during inspection. Our two stock controllers hold the block until final disposition is posted.

5. Damaged, leaking, suspect and temperature-abused units go to quarantine the same day they are found under PR-09. We label date, return reference, location and fault, move the same day to the quarantine area in Zone F respecting the 800 kg limit per pallet including load, and enter the move in the quarantine record as blocked stock. Such units are never re-cooled, re-racked, picked or dispatched before a decision. Hazmat returns stay only in the 60 m2 ventilated cage within the 4,000 kg limit.

6. After inspection of every unit we propose a single disposition per line. We propose restock to Zone B, C or E, rework at the value-added packing workstations, or scrap via quarantine, stating quantities, batch, expiry, condition and reason in the WMS and shift file. No unit leaves the inspection area on the proposer's authority alone.

7. No returned unit is restocked, reworked or scrapped until the shift supervisor approves the final disposition. The supervisor in charge reviews inspection result, proposal and system block and releases only passed, fully labelled stock with WMS licence for put-away under PR-02. Disposition and any write-off up to and including 500 EUR is approved on the shift; any case needing write-off above 500 EUR is secured, documented and passed to the warehouse manager the same day with no scrapping without that signature and no splitting to stay below the threshold.

8. Approved restock moves as booked stock without mixing. We collect only released, labelled pallets from Zone F, scan out of returns and into location, respecting the 2,700 kg rack-bay limit and the closed route with doors shut for Zone E.
